night.label: Declines to stay and eat
night.detail: Coworkers invited her to stay and eat; she said she had to get home for a 5:30 am start at her new job and was rushing home to bed.

night.label: Couple pass 1 east: no car
night.detail: The 2025 witness couple drive east toward the inn and see no car at the house.

night.label: Truck reported idling by covered bridge
night.detail: A volunteer searcher wrote of a report of a truck parked and idling by the second covered bridge, just before the Dutchburn place. Time and source not given.
night.conflict: Single secondhand report; the night window is assumed.

night.label: White pickup parked down the road
night.detail: Her parents were told of a white pickup parked down the road that night, and of a man flirting with her at the inn (Burlington Free Press, April 2004).
night.conflict: Hearsay relayed by the parents; time not given.

night.label: Couple stop to call, then turn back
night.detail: They stop where there is cell service, are invited to a party in St. Albans, debate it, and turn around to go.

night.label: Leaves the Black Lantern Inn
night.detail: She clocks out about 11:20. A coworker watches her walk alone to her car and drive out of the lot.
night.conflict: Lt. Nelson (2004): 'just before 11:30'; The Murder Squad hosts: 11:30-midnight.

night.label: Neighbours woken by a man shouting
night.detail: Neighbours about 600 ft away were woken by a man shouting, looked out, saw nothing and went back to bed. By 2019 the retelling was a scream.
night.conflict: Time never given; a 2006 family-forum timeline says the neighbour later retracted.

night.label: Turns left, toward home
night.detail: A coworker saw her turn left out of the lot, south-west on VT-118 toward East Berkshire, the way home, and toward the Dutchburn house 2.3 km away.

night.label: Earliest possible arrival at the house
night.detail: Inference: the house is 2.3 km by road, about 2-3 minutes' drive. No one on foot from the village could reach it by 11:30-11:45.
night.conflict: Analysis (OSRM and walk model), not a sighting.

night.label: Couple pass 2 west: car, lights on
night.detail: Heading west, the couple see her car at the house: headlights on, doors shut, nobody in sight.
night.conflict: Pass times rest on memory 21 years on; investigators give 11:30-11:45 overall.

night.label: Police get calls about the car
night.detail: An officer on duty that night said law enforcement got calls about the car during the night and treated it as routine.
night.conflict: Who called and when is only in dispatch logs.

night.label: Pass 3 east: man in the headlights
night.detail: Turning back to help, they see a tall, stocky man in a black hoodie standing in her headlights, a car door open. He turns his face aside and puts a hand up.

night.label: Silver Civic speeds in, brakes at scene
night.detail: A late-1990s or early-2000s grey or silver Honda Civic comes extremely fast from the east (inn side), nearly hits them, and is seen to hammer the brakes at the scene.
night.conflict: The PIs' 2025 poster says the Civic was 'headed north on Rte 118'; the recording says it came from the east.

night.label: Pass 4 west: nobody, door open
night.detail: Under two minutes later, after turning at a covered bridge: nobody there, the door open, the lights on.

night.label: Couple chase the Civic west
night.detail: They chase the Civic west toward Enosburg Falls and St. Albans at 65+ mph and cannot catch it. They came forward only after the 2024 reward.

night.label: 15°F, clear and calm
night.detail: Morrisville-Stowe ASOS (42 km south): 15°F at 11:54 pm, clear and calm. No precipitation overnight.

night.label: Witnesses to the car at midnight
night.detail: Overacker (2023) spoke of witnesses to the car at midnight.
night.conflict: Barry and Overacker (2022) put the earliest pre-2025 sighting at 12:15 or 12:30.

night.label: Blog version: second man sees turn signal
night.detail: Blog timelines and the 2011 Disappeared episode add a second man who saw a turn signal flashing at 12:00-12:30. The PIs place the signal at the ex-boyfriend's visit instead.
night.conflict: Round 4 correction: the PIs' recorded version is better sourced.

night.label: Passer-by: headlights on, nobody around
night.detail: The earliest sighting known before 2025: a male passer-by sees the car with headlights on and nobody around. Barry says 12:15, Overacker 12:30.
night.conflict: Repo earlier had ~11:45 from a secondhand summary; the witness himself said 11:30-12:30 (2019).

night.label: VSP: car seen 90 minutes after she left
night.detail: VSP (WCAX, 2016): eyewitnesses put the car at the farmhouse about an hour and a half after she left; Maj. Hall said whatever happened, happened very quickly.
night.conflict: The 2025 couple put the car there by about 11:30-11:45.

night.label: Trooper at the car at 1:22 am?
night.detail: AMW (Jan 2005) says a trooper radioed in at 1:22 am that he had found an empty car; Lt. Nelson (2004) said a neighbour discovered it around 1:22 a.m. Unconfirmed.
night.conflict: AMW's 2007 rewrite and all later sources say 1:30 pm dispatch; possibly AM/PM confusion, or a night visit plus afternoon tow. Only the dispatch log settles it.

night.label: Ex-boyfriend's first story: passed, kept going
night.detail: His first story to police: driving back from Canada he passed at 2:30, wasn't sure it was her car, and kept going. He later said this was a lie.
night.conflict: Another early version had him stop at 2:30, find lights on and doors open, and shut them.

night.label: Ex-boyfriend shuts doors, turns lights off
night.detail: His later version: about 4:30, after using drugs at another house, he found lights on, both doors open and a directional on; turned off the lights, shut both doors, touched nothing else, and left.
night.conflict: Times varied (2:30 or 4:30); the signal appears only in the PIs' retellings. PIs and VSP say he was not involved.

night.label: Battery likely flat by 4:30
night.detail: Analysis: with the engine off, headlights since about 11:30 would very likely have flattened a 1985 battery by 4:30, so 'lights on' fits an earlier time or a running engine.
night.conflict: Analysis, not a sighting; depends on engine state.

night.label: Misses 5:30 am start at new job
night.detail: She was due at 5:30 am for her first day at a new job, by one account KJ's Diner in St. Albans. No source says the job called anyone.
night.conflict: KJ's as the job comes from one 2016 Websleuths poster (C).

night.label: Sunrise; 8°F with valley mist
night.detail: Sunrise 5:53 am; moonrise 6:07 am. Morrisville-Stowe read 8°F at 5:54 am with mist.

night.label: VSP gets abandoned-car report
night.detail: On the morning of 20 March VSP received a report of an abandoned car, reported by a passer-by, at the 'Old Dutchburn Barn'.
night.conflict: Round 9: the trooper responded to a report; he did not come on it by chance. WND (2006) said a trooper on patrol spotted it.

night.label: 'A slew of people' drive past
night.detail: Overacker: between morning and 1 pm many drivers must have passed the car in plain view; as far as is known none reported it besides the morning caller.
night.conflict: Overacker's inference.

night.label: News crew at the car?
night.detail: A volunteer searcher said a news crew was at the car around 9:30 am. NBC5's March 2004 film shows the house after the tow.
night.conflict: NBC5's footage shows the house after the tow with a poster on the window, which argues against a morning visit.

night.label: Travellers photograph the scene
night.detail: Three out-of-state skiers from Jay Peak stop and take the only public photos. Camera clock: 10:14:37 and 10:15:23 am. The road photos show the car's passenger side.
night.conflict: Corrected from 7-8:30 am (later retellings); clock confirmed by a 2017 PI account and their own 2005 answers.

night.label: Travellers: door unlocked, items on ground
night.detail: One opened a door (window up, unlocked). By the driver's door: a metallic necklace, a to-go mug and about $0.65 in change within five feet. Food on the back seat; no keys, no skid marks.

night.label: Squeezed lime wedge on the trunk
night.detail: The travellers reported a squeezed lime wedge on the trunk; it was never collected. Fast-food wrappers inside.
night.conflict: Their account only, absent from 2004 press; present in their 2005 answers.

night.label: Travellers' friends start into the house
night.detail: One traveller (2025): his friends started to climb into the house; on the way they had passed a barn on fire near Sheldon. VSP took statements from two of them a week or two later.
night.conflict: No barn fire is in NFIRS for 20 March, though several nearby departments did not report.

night.label: Light snow begins
night.detail: Light snow begins on and off into the evening. Until then, any tracks had sat untouched for about 12 hours on bare grass near the house and snow further out.
night.conflict: The travellers recalled 11:00 am; airport reports put it at 11:30 am-noon.

night.label: Trooper finds car backed into house
night.detail: Dispatched trooper finds the car backed into the gable, rear hung on the foundation, plywood on the trunk; wheels cut hard left; lights off; doors shut, unlocked; no keys.
night.conflict: A poster says dispatched at 1:30 pm; AMW (2005) and Kates (2009) had a 1:22-1:30 am log.

night.label: Trooper checks house, moves items into car
night.detail: He checks the farmhouse and finds no one, notes two uncashed Black Lantern paychecks (under $150), and picks items off the ground, the necklace among them, putting them in the car.

night.label: Car towed to a local garage
night.detail: Assuming a drunk driver abandoned it, he has it towed; one account says logged as a possible hit-and-run. He drives to the inn, finds it closed, and goes on a long weekend.
night.conflict: A 2006 family-forum timeline says the tow was Monday 22 March at the property overseer's request.

night.label: Family not notified
night.detail: Police reportedly tried to phone the registered owner, her mother, and failed. VSP: the trooper went to the restaurant instead and assumed the owner would ask where the car was.
night.conflict: The failed phone call is grade C.

looks.people: a tall, heavy man in the headlights, face turned
a grey Civic speeds in from the east and brakes at the scene
no one; a turn signal on; he shuts doors and lights
no one; food inside; lime on the trunk
no keys; change and necklace on the ground

objects.name: Car backed into abandoned house
objects.observed: Her 1985 Oldsmobile 88 was found backed into the side of the abandoned Dutchburn house on VT-118, about a mile from the inn.
objects.disputes: FBI poster says barn; all others say house.
objects.why: VSP and FBI both state it; every account agrees on the back-in.

objects.name: Rear hung on foundation
objects.observed: The rear bumper was stuck on the house foundation with the rear tyres lifted, so the rear-drive car could not move.
objects.why: Othram wrote it from the VSP file; matches PI accounts and the underside gouge.

objects.name: Plywood fallen onto trunk
objects.observed: A sheet of plywood that had covered a window lay on the trunk when the trooper arrived.
objects.why: Several PI retellings agree; no official text found.

objects.name: Car punched hole in house
objects.observed: The investigator says the car punched a hole in the building; the 2004 lead officer called damage to the car minimal.
objects.disputes: Severity unclear: 'hole' vs 'minimal' damage; impact speed still open per VSP.
objects.why: PI paraphrase plus 2004 police quote; sizes never measured.

objects.name: Front wheels cut hard left
objects.observed: The trooper found the front wheels cut hard to the driver's side; a head-on photo shows the same.
objects.disputes: Who turned them is unknown: driver trying to escape, or position left from the back-in.
objects.why: PI narration from trooper and photos; consistent across tellings.

objects.name: Lights off, doors shut, unlocked
objects.observed: At the afternoon visit the headlights were off and the doors were closed but unlocked.
objects.why: Othram confirms unlocked; the ex-boyfriend says he shut doors and lights.

objects.name: Keys missing, never found
objects.observed: No keys were in or around the car; metal detectors in the yard and cornfield never found them.
objects.disputes: Tow company first said it had the keys, then said there never were any.
objects.why: Official; slightly lowered by the tow firm's first answer that it had them.

objects.name: Tow firm's two key answers
objects.observed: At the impound the towing company first told her father it had the keys, then said there never were any.
objects.why: First-hand from her father, recorded; the firm's own record is not public.

objects.name: Car may start without key
objects.observed: Sources told a PI the car could be started without a key; her father says its locking column needed one.
objects.disputes: Father: locking column ignition, needed a key.
objects.why: Hearsay, one item an online chat screenshot; owner's father disputes it.

objects.name: No skid marks, few grass marks
objects.observed: No skid marks; just a few marks in the grass; no sign the car left the road out of control.
objects.why: PI and travellers agree; nobody measured the scene.

objects.name: Matted grass from 100 ft past
objects.observed: Her father saw matted grass from about 100 feet past the house right up to the car, so the car went past and reversed.
objects.disputes: Repo once wrote 'before' the house; corrected to 'past'.
objects.why: First-hand but observed days later, after tow and searches.

objects.name: Seat set for her size
objects.observed: A volunteer searcher who sat in the car in spring 2005 found the power seat still set for someone her size.
objects.disputes: A PI informant said a tall man drove it with the seat forward.
objects.why: Observed a year later, after lab and family; seat may have been moved.

objects.name: 2005 look: fuel, engine, wiper
objects.observed: A volunteer who examined the car in spring 2005 found fuel in the tank, the engine untouched, and the driver's wiper jammed under the sill.
objects.why: Single blog source, a year later; no gauge reading published.

objects.name: Fuel tank gouge, exhaust dent
objects.observed: Underside photo shows a gouge in the fuel tank and a dented exhaust, fitting the rear riding onto the foundation.
objects.disputes: The car already had marks and dents from an earlier accident.
objects.why: Photo exists in repo, but prior damage cannot be excluded.

objects.name: Car released, later junked
objects.observed: VSP released the car to her parents in late September 2004; it was later junked, so seat, gear and fuel survive only in records.
objects.why: Father and PI firm agree; exact junk date single-sourced.

objects.name: Gear and seat never recorded
objects.observed: Gear, ignition and seat position were never recorded (PIs); VSP's case officer says police took about one photo, the passer-by documented it better.
objects.disputes: Mother was shown police photos of the car by ~25 Mar 2004.
objects.why: PI statement; VSP's own notes are not public.

objects.name: Two uncashed paychecks left
objects.observed: Two uncashed Black Lantern paychecks, under $150 in all, lay on the seat.
objects.why: Trooper, NBC and VSP's case officer all cite them.

objects.name: ATM card, glasses, meds left
objects.observed: Her father found her ATM card, glasses, contact lens case and migraine medication inside the returned car.
objects.disputes: Mother (29 Mar 2004): ATM card, medication and contacts were at the friend's house.
objects.why: First-hand, but mother said in March 2004 these were at the friend's house.

objects.name: Driver's license location unclear
objects.observed: Parents said in March 2004 she left her license at the friend's house; a Sept 2004 TV report put it in the car.
objects.disputes: House (parents, Mar 2004) vs car (WPTZ Sep 2004; podcast hosts 2020).
objects.why: Two grade-B reports conflict; the property log would settle it.

objects.name: Loose change on the ground
objects.observed: Loose change lay on the ground by the car; travellers put about $0.65 near the driver's door.
objects.disputes: VSP: items on the ground may not have come from her car.
objects.why: Trooper and travellers both saw coins; VSP warns roadside litter is common.

objects.name: Necklace on the ground
objects.observed: A metallic costume-style necklace lay on the ground outside the driver's door; the trooper later put it in the car.
objects.disputes: Barry 2025: 'we don't actually know' it was hers.
objects.why: Seen by trooper and travellers; ownership and whether broken not confirmed.

objects.name: Trooper moved ground items
objects.observed: The trooper picked items off the ground, the necklace among them, and put them in the car before any record.
objects.why: PI-recounted, echoed by a 2006 press piece; positions lost.

objects.name: Fast-food wrappers and food
objects.observed: Fast-food wrappers and food inside; unopened non-perishable food on the back seat.
objects.disputes: Some lists add beer bottles and Solo cups (C).
objects.why: Travellers via PIs; several later inventories agree.

objects.name: Half-eaten burrito container
objects.observed: A styrofoam takeout container with a half-eaten burrito sat on the passenger floor.
objects.why: Podcast hosts and a volunteer's blog only; origin of food unknown.

objects.name: Squeezed lime wedge on trunk
objects.observed: A squeezed lime wedge sat on the trunk; never collected.
objects.disputes: Absent from all 2004 press; position (plywood or metal) unknown.
objects.why: Travellers' account only, but already in their 2005 answers.

objects.name: To-go mug on the ground
objects.observed: A convenience-store refillable to-go mug lay within about five feet of the change and necklace.
objects.why: One traveller's 2005 written answers, relayed by a blog.

objects.name: Woman's fleece jacket nearby
objects.observed: Her father found a woman's small fleece jacket near the scene after the police search, with a wallet full of Canadian money and another woman's ID.
objects.disputes: Charley Project: 'in a field', unsourced.
objects.why: Contemporaneous 2004 press; VSP later found the owner and judged it unconnected.

objects.name: Jacket owner found, unconnected
objects.observed: VSP's case officer said they found the jacket's owner and it wasn't connected.
objects.why: Investigator on the record; when and where it was lost not public.

objects.name: 26 Mar search items
objects.observed: The VSP K-9 and helicopter search found loose change, a water bottle, an unsmoked cigarette and an item of interest.
objects.disputes: PIs: the unlit cigarette is an unconfirmed rumour.
objects.why: Press of the search; the PIs call the cigarette an unconfirmed rumour.

objects.name: K-9 item DNA: uninvolved man
objects.observed: DNA on the K-9 item was traced via genealogy to a man with no involvement; it matched none of 11 persons of interest or CODIS.
objects.why: VSP release; VSP 2024 adds it was near, not at, the scene.

objects.name: In-car DNA from known people
objects.observed: In-car DNA matched an earlier ex-boyfriend and close friends; a latent print matched a friend's hand.
objects.disputes: VSP 2016 announced DNA found in the car with no detail.
objects.why: PI narration citing a 2014 lab report; VSP took 'very little' DNA.

objects.name: Police took little DNA
objects.observed: Police took very little DNA from the car and later changed policy to keep such cars.
objects.why: Her father and PIs; consistent with the car being released and junked.

objects.name: PI firm: armrest blood spots
objects.observed: A private firm says it found three blood spots under the driver's armrest by alternate light, plus a syringe cap and green fibres, after the car's release.
objects.disputes: VSP (Jun 2004): forensic testing revealed no evidence; volunteer saw no blood.
objects.why: One firm's own claim; testing never reported; VSP 2004 said testing found nothing.

objects.name: PI firm: cuffs, underwear finds
objects.observed: The same firm says it found cut flex-cuffs with an 18-inch hair, women's underwear her size and a syringe near the scene, signed for by VSP.
objects.why: Single-party claim repeated 2017 and 2025; no test result public.

objects.name: Shoes on VT-118 shoulder
objects.observed: A pair of shoes was photographed on the VT-118 shoulder about two blocks from the house, pointing toward it.
objects.why: Firm's photo and caption only; never tied to her.

objects.name: Volunteer finds: knife, tape, hair
objects.observed: Volunteers found a purple T-shirt, a knife, a large spoon and tape that looked to have hair on it near the car.
objects.why: One TV report; two weeks after; litter likely; never mentioned again.

objects.name: Later finds, none hers
objects.observed: Later searches found jeans off Gibou Road (2007, not hers) and an old sweatshirt in leaves; nothing linked to her.
objects.why: Press and VSP 2024 interview agree nothing tied to her.

objects.name: Left inn alone ~11:20 pm
objects.observed: The owner's wife watched her get in alone about 11:20 and drive out; nobody drove out after her. A coworker saw her turn left, toward home.
objects.disputes: Lead officer 2004: 'just before 11:30'. The turn-left detail is a blog relay (C).
objects.why: VSP and all accounts agree; watcher's view of the street is limited.

objects.name: Uneventful shift, no calls
objects.observed: Coworkers said her shift was uneventful: no visitors, no calls made or received, and she was not upset or anxious.
objects.why: From the VSP file via Othram; inn phone records also led nowhere.

objects.name: Couple: no car at 11:00
objects.observed: Driving east about 11:00 pm, the couple saw no car at the house.
objects.why: Recalled 21 years later, retold by the PIs.

objects.name: Couple: lights on, doors shut
objects.observed: Heading west, the couple saw her car at the house with headlights on, doors shut, and no one in sight.
objects.disputes: VSP 2016: eyewitnesses put the car there ~1.5 h after she left.
objects.why: Simulator weight 0.7; vivid memory, long delay, PI retelling.

objects.name: Man in her headlights
objects.observed: Turning back east, the couple saw a tall stocky man in a black hoodie in her headlights with a door open; he turned his face and raised a hand.
objects.disputes: Pre-2025 first passer-by saw nobody near the car.
objects.why: Core of their account; simulator weight 0.65; 21-year recall.

objects.name: Silver Civic brakes at scene
objects.observed: A late-1990s grey or silver Honda, believed a Civic, came fast from the east, nearly hit them, and braked hard at the scene.
objects.disputes: Simulator found the Civic likelier uninvolved or misremembered (88%).
objects.why: Make and model at night, 21 years on; 'a very fleeting image'.

objects.name: Couple: nobody; chased Civic west
objects.observed: Under two minutes later, heading west: nobody there, door open, lights on. They chased the Civic west toward Enosburg Falls at 65+ mph and lost it.
objects.disputes: One flyer says the Civic was headed north on VT-118.
objects.why: Same witnesses and caveats as the earlier passes.

objects.name: Passer-by ~12:15: nobody
objects.observed: A male passer-by saw the car with headlights on and nobody around at about 12:15-12:30; by 2023 the PIs knew four overnight witnesses.
objects.disputes: Barry 2025 said the earliest sighting was ~11:45.
objects.why: PI-recorded; time varies 11:30-12:30 by source.

objects.name: Police got calls overnight
objects.observed: An officer on duty said law enforcement got calls about the car during the night and treated it as routine.
objects.why: Secondhand via PIs; no dispatch log public.

objects.name: Trooper at car ~1:22 am?
objects.observed: America's Most Wanted (Jan 2005) and the 2004 lead officer put a trooper or report at the car about 1:22 a.m.
objects.disputes: Later AMW text and all later sources: 1:30 p.m. dispatch.
objects.why: Two early sources say a.m.; later sources say p.m.; log unseen.

objects.name: Neighbours woke to man shouting
objects.observed: Neighbours near the scene were woken by a man shouting, looked out, saw nothing, went back to bed. Time never given.
objects.disputes: Retold as 'a scream' by 2019; a 2006 forum says retracted.
objects.why: 2004 press via her mother; later 'retracted'; simulator weight 0.3.

objects.name: Told: white pickup, flirting man
objects.observed: In April 2004 her parents were told of a white pickup parked down the road that night and a man flirting with her at the inn.
objects.why: Secondhand report in 2004 press; no time, place or follow-up.

objects.name: Truck idling by covered bridge
objects.observed: A truck was reported parked and idling by the second covered bridge just before the Dutchburn place.
objects.why: Blog relay, unsourced; colour never determined.

objects.name: Ex-boyfriend: doors open, lights on
objects.observed: The ex-boyfriend said he found lights on and both doors open, turned off the lights, shut the doors, touched nothing else.
objects.disputes: First told VSP he passed at 2:30 and kept going; later said ~4:30.
objects.why: His stories changed often; simulator weight 0.3; police believe him uninvolved.

objects.name: A directional on (rumour)
objects.observed: PI shorthand says a directional or blinker was on at the ex-boyfriend's visit; his own retold interview mentions none.
objects.disputes: Blogs give it to a second man at 12:00-12:30; one poster says left signal.
objects.why: Rumour-grade: absent from both first-hand retellings.

objects.name: Lights on at 4:30 strains battery
objects.observed: Modelled: with the engine off, headlights would very likely be flat well before 4:30 am.
objects.why: Physics with assumed loads; not a measurement of this battery.

objects.name: Car reported that morning
objects.observed: VSP received a report of an abandoned car on the morning of 20 March; a passer-by reported it.
objects.disputes: Caller and time not public.
objects.why: From the VSP file via Othram and a 2024 VSP briefing.

objects.name: Travellers photographed scene ~10:15
objects.observed: Three travellers stopped and photographed the car; camera clock 10:14-10:15 am; their camera is in VSP evidence.
objects.disputes: Retold later as 7-8:30 am.
objects.why: Photos exist; time has three agreeing sources; clock unverified.

objects.name: A traveller opened a door
objects.observed: One traveller opened a door; window up, door unlocked; friends started into the house.
objects.disputes: VSP officer 2020: they 'didn't touch anything'.
objects.why: Their own 2005 and 2025 accounts via blog and Reddit.

objects.name: Bare grass at the house
objects.observed: In the photos the ground right around the house looked like bare grass, with snow further out in the field.
objects.disputes: Weather stations show a 1-3 inch cover regionally.
objects.why: PI reading of photos; tracks would show only as matted grass.

objects.name: No tracks reported, no cameras
objects.observed: No public source reports footprints or second-vehicle tracks; a host says photo tracks were studied. There were no cameras anywhere.
objects.why: Absence of report, not proof of absence; ground mostly bare.

objects.name: Trooper arrives ~1:15-1:30 pm
objects.observed: A trooper, dispatched about 1:30 pm, found the car, assumed a drunk driver, had it towed, found the inn closed and went on a long weekend.
objects.disputes: Tow may have been Monday 22 Mar at the property overseer's request (2006 forum).
objects.why: PIs and posters agree; trooper's notes not public.

objects.name: Snow began late Saturday morning
objects.observed: Light snow began about 11:00-11:30 am Saturday, after the travellers passed; more fell 21-22 Mar and 4-6 Apr.
objects.why: Airport observations plus a traveller's own 2005 account agree.

objects.name: No body in 22 years
objects.observed: No remains have been found; a 78-case screen of unidentified remains found no match.
objects.why: Official missing-person status; screen is ours, on public data.

objects.name: No confirmed sign of life
objects.observed: No confirmed sighting since; the only notable lookalike (Atlantic City, Jan 2006) was judged not her.
objects.why: VSP 2024: last reported sighting 15+ years ago; dismissed.

objects.name: No cell phone or purse
objects.observed: Her father says she had no cell phone and no purse; she kept things in her pockets.
objects.disputes: VSP case officer 2020: 'She would have taken her purse.'
objects.why: First-hand family knowledge; VSP officer thinks she had a purse.

objects.name: No cell service at house
objects.observed: The PIs say there was no cell service at the house; service existed elsewhere on that stretch.
objects.disputes: Volunteer: Tracfone had '3 bars at least' at the house (2005).
objects.why: PIs consistent; a volunteer's 2005 phone showed bars there.

objects.name: Not reported missing till 23 Mar
objects.observed: Reported missing on 23 March; the roommate and parents each assumed she was with the other.
objects.disputes: Roommate may have seen the note Sunday night, not Monday.
objects.why: Consistent across press.

objects.name: No underwater river search
objects.observed: The Trout River banks and surface were searched; no diver or underwater search of it is on record.
objects.why: Absence in the public record; VSP may hold more.

objects.name: Disposal tips, serial killer: closed
objects.observed: Pig-farm, wood-chopper and manure-pit stories were checked and none corroborated; the FBI ruled out a known serial killer in 2012.
objects.why: VSP case officer on the record.

objects.name: 5:30 am start next morning
objects.observed: Next morning was her first day at a new St. Albans diner job, starting 5:30 am; she was 'rushing home to get in bed'.
objects.disputes: Father: worked there 'one day'; PIs 2019: 'a couple weeks'.
objects.why: PI recorded; job length varies by account.

objects.name: Note, GED, plans: expected home
objects.observed: She left a note with her shift (out 10 pm-12) and schedule through the 28th. She had passed her GED, worked two jobs, planned another car.
objects.why: Roommate found it undisturbed; quoted consistently.

objects.name: Assault case hearing 9 Apr
objects.observed: She was assaulted at a party on 27 Feb; charges filed, hearing set for 9 Apr; the other party is not a suspect.
objects.disputes: 2004 mother: 'a group of girls'; later accounts: one assailant.
objects.why: Press plus VSP 2020; first reports say a group of girls.

objects.name: Shaken outside St. Albans store
objects.observed: In a St. Albans store something outside caught her attention; she left and came back shaken and agitated.
objects.disputes: A blog says it was a mall, meeting back at the car.
objects.why: Mother's account; PI reads it as a cigarette break and friction.

objects.name: Car broken into twice at diner
objects.observed: Her car was broken into twice at the St. Albans diner job in the weeks before.
objects.why: PI statement only; what was taken or reported unknown.

objects.name: Few knew she worked there
objects.observed: VSP: very few people knew she worked at the inn; she had been ostracized by friends. Her routine was weeks old: second weekend at the inn.
objects.why: Investigator's judgement on the record.

objects.name: Reported runaway once, 2003
objects.observed: VSP said in 2004 that her father had reported her missing once before, in 2003, as a runaway.
objects.disputes: Family: 'not a runaway'; VSP dropped the runaway listing by June 2004.
objects.why: VSP/NHSP release via repost and 2004 press.

objects.name: Police: owed a dealer money
objects.observed: In June 2004 police said she had become a drug user and buyer and owed a dealer money; by 2008 VSP called much of it rumour.
objects.disputes: VSP 2008: 'Much of this information can be attributed to rumors'.
objects.why: VSP itself later could not substantiate it.

objects.name: Berkshire raid: no sign of her
objects.observed: On a tip she was held there, police raided a Berkshire house on 15 Apr 2004; drugs found, no sign of her.
objects.why: Press; PIs see zero evidence the men were involved.

objects.name: Affidavit: body on pig farm
objects.observed: A 2006 affidavit claimed she was killed over money, kept in a basement and disposed of on a pig farm.
objects.disputes: Dated late 2004 in early repo notes; VSP says 2006.
objects.why: Never corroborated; its supposed source denies it; credibility questioned from the start.

objects.name: New moon, no natural light
objects.observed: The moon was about 1% lit and below the horizon all night; very few streetlights on that road.
objects.disputes: A volunteer blog claims a street lamp across from the house.
objects.why: Ephemeris computation checked against USNO; VSP on lighting.

objects.name: Clear, calm, 15 F, dusting
objects.observed: Clear and calm; 15 F near midnight, 8 F by dawn; a fresh dusting on 1-3 inches of cover; no precipitation overnight.
objects.disputes: A 2006 forum timeline claims 'blizzardy showers'.
objects.why: NOAA/ASOS and co-op data; nearest hourly station 42 km away.

objects.name: House not a hangout
objects.observed: PI: nobody stopped or partied at the house; that was asked of everybody.
objects.disputes: Blogs: 'druggie hangout'; VSP 2020: some say a meeting place.
objects.why: PI canvass; VSP officer says opinions differ on a meeting place.

objects.name: House searched, details unknown
objects.observed: The trooper found nobody inside the farmhouse on 20 Mar; family, police and teams searched it several times; no word on the cellar.
objects.why: Father's forum post and PI statement agree; scope unknown.

objects.name: River forensics behind barn
objects.observed: Police did forensic evaluations along the river behind the barn in early May 2004.
objects.why: One contemporaneous TV report; reason and result unknown.

objects.name: Police: foul play likely
objects.observed: Within months police concluded foul play was likely; posters say foul play suspected; no evidence she ran.
objects.disputes: June 2004 WNNE wording 'no evidence of foul play'.
objects.why: Official stance; reasoning rests on items left and no contact.

objects.name: Residence of interest nearby
objects.observed: A residence within walking distance with 'some connection' is under review.
objects.why: PIs mention it without detail.

objects.name: Lone inn guest cleared
objects.observed: A man holidaying alone at the inn that night was interviewed; VSP and the PI are confident he is not involved.
objects.why: PI and VSP view; basis not public.

objects.name: Walker from inn arrives too late
objects.observed: Modelled: the 2.27 km walk takes about 27 minutes, so nobody leaving the inn with her on foot reaches the car by 11:30-11:45.
objects.why: Measured route and standard walking speeds; running is possible.

objects.name: Physics: deliberate back-in fits
objects.observed: Car-only physics: a slow deliberate back-in reaches the photo pose 6-56 times as often as a fearful reverse.
objects.disputes: PIs 2022: 'threw it in reverse, hit the gas'.
objects.why: Simulation with assumed parameters; no slope modelled.

meta.title: Regional offenders, unsolved series and disappearances (scope around Montgomery, VT)
meta.scope: About 350 km of Montgomery (VT, NH, western ME, northern NY, western MA north of the Pike, southern QC, eastern ON); offenders active 1980-2010 or living in the region in 2004. single_abduction: convicted killers of a girl or young woman (13-30) taken by stranger or roadside approach 1995-2010 within ~200 km. disappearance_unsolved: women 13-30 missing 1995-2010.
meta.distance_method: Haversine great-circle distance (R = 6371.0088 km) from 44.90 N, 72.64 W to each place; distance_km is the minimum over an entry's offence, residence or last-seen places (places marked counts_for_distance=false, such as a surrender site, are listed but not used). Place coordinates are approximate town or neighbourhood centroids.
meta.status_values: status_on_2004_03_19 is the offender's status on 19 Mar 2004. For missing persons and unsolved series it is 'unknown'; status_note says when the person disappeared after that date.
meta.scope_flag: Non-null when an entry falls outside the stated criteria (distance, date or age) and is kept for a stated reason.
meta.caution: Inclusion means only that an entry meets the geographic and date criteria. Nothing here suggests that anyone listed is connected to Brianna Maitland. No uncharged suspect is named. Convicted facts come from court reporting, police statements or encyclopedias; weaker sourcing is marked medium or low.
meta.notes_file: Research notes with sources and exclusions were kept outside the repo (research_regional.md in the session scratchpad).

local_history.scope: Montgomery, Vermont (Franklin County) and neighbours; local history context, settlement to 2004. Context only.

timeline.title: Hazen's military road stops at Hazen's Notch
timeline.text: Before anyone settled the town, the Revolutionary War military road begun by Jacob Bayley in 1776 and pushed on by Gen. Moses Hazen in 1779 was abandoned at the notch that now bears Hazen's name; the 1991 National Register form says Route 118 was first built as part of this road.

sources.quote: By late summer, Hazen had reached the notch that now bears his name in the Green Mountains near Westfield where work was halted still some forty miles short of the road's intended destination, St. Johns, Canada.
Route 118, originally constructed as part of the Hazen Road (built from 1776-1779 to move Revolutionary War troops to invade Canada)

timeline.title: Township granted by the Vermont legislature
timeline.text: The legislature of the independent Vermont republic granted a six-mile-square township of 23,040 acres to Stephen R. Bradley, the Rev. Ezra Stiles and associates; the charter text gives 15 March 1780, while the 19th-century county histories and the town plan say 13 March.

sources.quote: The aforesaid Grant was made by the Legislature of this State on the 15th day of March, 1780
sources.note: Transcribed by the Montgomery Historical Society from H. A. Black, State Papers of Vermont: Charters, vol. II (1922), pp. 138-9.

sources.quote: granted by the State, March 13, 1780, to Stephen R. Bradley, Rev. Ezra Stiles, John Graham, and others to the number of sixty-four, though it did not receive its charter until October 8, 1789.
Montgomery was named in honor of General Richard Montgomery (1738–1775), an Revolutionary War leader who was the first American general to die in battle.

timeline.title: Charter sealed
timeline.text: Nine years after the grant, Governor Thomas Chittenden's council sealed the charter of Montgomery, which still had no settlers.

sources.quote: In Testimony whereof we have caused the Seal of this State to be affixed in Council this 8th day of October A.D. 1789
The township was granted Mar. 13, 1780, to Stephen R. Bradley, Rev. Ezra Stiles, D. D., John Graham, and others, but was not chartered until Oct. 1789.

timeline.title: First permanent settler
timeline.text: Capt. Joshua Clapp, a Revolutionary War officer, brought his family from Worcester County, Massachusetts, in March (or spring) 1793 and took up land on both sides of the Trout River; his son Joel, born 14 September 1793, was the first child born in the town.

sources.quote: The first permanent settlement in Montgomery was made by Joshua Clapp, in March, 1793.
The first permanent settlement was made by Capt. Joshua Clapp, a revolutionary officer of much respectability, who removed his family from Worcester Co., Mass. in the spring of 1793.
His son, Joel, was the first child born in the town, September 14, 1793.

timeline.title: Town organized at the first town meeting
timeline.text: The freemen met at Joshua Clapp's house and chose the first town officers, with Samuel Barnard as town clerk.

sources.quote: the freemen met at the dwelling house of Joshua Clapp, at one o'clock in the afternoon on August 12, 1802, for the purpose of choosing officers in pursuance of the petition.
The town was organized and the first town meeting held, August 12, 1802, when Samuel Barnard was chosen town clerk

timeline.title: The brick inn on the green is built (c.1803)
timeline.text: The two-and-a-half-storey brick hotel later called the Montgomery House (today the Black Lantern Inn) is reputed to date from 1803, making it one of the oldest buildings standing in the town.

sources.quote: The Montgomery House is reputed to have been built in 1803, one of the earliest buildings in the town still in existence.

timeline.title: State market road laid out through Hazen's Notch
timeline.text: A legislative committee adopted the travelled road through Montgomery and Hazen's Notch as part of a state market road; before the railways, farmers of north-eastern Vermont hauled butter and cheese over it to Montreal in winter.

sources.quote: have examined the present traveled road through the town of Montgomery leading through Hazen's Notch by Lusk's tavern, and Fassett's, Samuel Barnard's, and Henry N. Janes's, and have established the same as a part of said market road
sources.note: Certificate dated at Montgomery, June 23, 1821.

sources.quote: Before the advent of railroads in Northern Vermont this highway was much used by the people of Northeastern Vermont in the winter season, who transported their produce, butter, and cheese to Montreal

timeline.title: Butter-tub making begins (c.1842-44)
timeline.text: Merchant Asa Wheeler, who also built a starch factory and grist-mill, financed the cooper Joseph Hutchins in making turned spruce butter tubs, the trade that came to define the town's mills.

sources.quote: The butter tub industry began to attract attention in this town about the years 1842 to 1844
the first persons to engage in the business on that principle in this town, and probably in the state, were Asa Wheeler and Joseph Hutchins
He built a starch factory and grist-mill, and also the first butter-tub factory in the town.

timeline.title: Town enlarged to the south
timeline.text: A 1858 act, ratified by the voters of Montgomery and Lowell in March 1859, added about 7,000 acres from Lowell and Avery's Gore; a further part of Avery's Gore joined the town in 1963.

sources.quote: The act of the legislature in 1858, setting portions of the town of Lowell and Avery's Gore to the town of Montgomery, was ratified by the voters of the towns of Montgomery and Lowell, respectively, at their town meeting in March, 1859.
sources.note: OCR reads "IMarch".

sources.quote: In the year 1859 a tract, containing about 7000 acres from the town of Lowell and Avery's Gore, was added to it on the south
In 1963, part of Avery's Gore in Franklin County became part of Montgomery, with the other section becoming part of Belvidere in Lamoille County.

timeline.title: Longley Bridge: the oldest dated Jewett bridge
timeline.text: Brothers Sheldon and Savannah (or Savanard) Jewett of West Hill completed the Town-lattice Longley Bridge over the Trout River north-west of the village.

sources.quote: they completed the Longley Bridge in 1863, the oldest among their bridges whose dates are known.

timeline.town: St. Albans (with Sheldon and Enosburg Falls)
timeline.title: St. Albans Raid
timeline.text: Confederate raiders from Canada robbed the St. Albans banks, killed a resident and fled back across the border; the 1891 county history says their retreat ran through Sheldon and over the Missisquoi at Enosburg Falls.

sources.quote: Taking place in St. Albans, Vermont, on October 19, 1864, it was a raid conducted out of the Province of Canada by 21 Confederate soldiers
where they crossed the river at Enosburgh Falls and rode rapidly towards Canada.
sources.note: Aldrich dates the passage through Sheldon to "November 19, 1864", an error for 19 October.

timeline.title: Fenian raids across the Franklin County border
timeline.text: Irish-American Fenians gathered at St. Albans and Franklin and on 7 June 1866 crossed into Canada at Pigeon Hill; a second raid from Franklin was repulsed at Eccles Hill on 25 May 1870, and people from Berkshire went to Franklin to watch the 'army'.

sources.quote: On Wednesday, the 6th of June, the army concentrated and rendezvoused in the quiet town of Franklin
on June 7, 1866 Spear and his 1,000 to 1,500 men marched into Canada under the Green Irish flag, and occupied Pigeon Hill (called the Pigeon Hill Raid), Frelighsburg, St. Armand and Stanbridge.
The Fenians were overwhelmed by local militia units and armed citizens on May 25, 1870
to which place many Berkshire people then made a visit and enjoyed the pleasure the occasion afforded.

timeline.title: The Missisquoi Railroad opens; East Berkshire becomes Montgomery's station
timeline.text: The first train ran from Sheldon on 4 July 1870 on the Missisquoi Railroad, about 28 miles from St. Albans to Richford (where a line into Canada, the Southeastern, was built in 1871); no railway reached Montgomery, whose freight was hauled five miles to East Berkshire.

sources.quote: The first train from Sheldon was on the 4th of July, 1870, and regular trains were soon after put on.
which extended from the village of St. Albans to the village of Richford, a distance of about twenty-eight miles.
The first road was built in 1871, called the Southeastern.
five miles from the railroad station at East Berkshire on the Missisquoi Railroad
The railroad stop in East Berkshire, five miles northwest of the hotel, was a boon to business.

timeline.title: Hopkins Bridge built just over the Enosburg line
timeline.text: The Jewett brothers built the 91-foot Hopkins Bridge over the Trout River, the longest of their seven surviving bridges.

sources.quote: built the Hopkins Bridg in 1875.
sources.note: OCR drops the final "e" of "Bridge" at the line end.

sources.quote: Built in 1875 by brothers Sheldon & Savannah Jewett, it is one of a cluster of area covered bridges all attributed to the same builders.

timeline.title: Kendall's Spavin Cure and the patent-medicine boom
timeline.text: B. J. Kendall & Co. was formed in 1879 to market a remedy for lame horses, Kendall's Spavin Cure; its laboratory went up in 1880, and by 1891 five patent-medicine firms made it Enosburg Falls' chief industry.

sources.quote: with the result that the latter became interested in the business under the firm style of B. J. Kendall & Co., in the year 1879.
spavin cure laboratory, located at the Falls, was erected in 1880, for the manufacture of this remedy, ranking as one of the largest industries of the county.
are proprietary or patent medicines ; and in this special industry Enosburgh Falls has a reputation second to no place in the state.

timeline.title: The turn to dairying
timeline.text: Butter output rose from over 35,000 lb in 1870 to 180,000 lb in 1880, according to census figures compiled by the Montgomery Historical Society; Hemenway's 1871 sketch already praised the town's pasture, dairy and Timothy grass seed.

sources.quote: By 1880 Montgomery farms produced 180,000 pounds of butter, an over 5 fold increase in just 10 years.
Montgomery is celebrated for its rich pasturage, producing fine cattle, horses, and sheep, and its dairy products rank among the best.

timeline.title: Comstock and Hutchins bridges; a town of tub mills
timeline.text: The Jewetts completed the Comstock and Hutchins bridges (the town plan also dates the Creamery/West Hill and Hectorville bridges to 1883), while the county gazetteer listed several butter-tub factories, the largest able to make 175,000 tubs a year.

sources.quote: they completed the Comstock Bridge in 1883.
they completed the Hutchins Bridge in 1883.
The mill is operated by water-power and has the capacity for manufacturing 175,000 butter-tubs per year and cutting 12,000 feet of lumber per day.

timeline.title: Bobbin factory at Black Falls
timeline.text: J. E. Smith & Co. opened a mill turning rough bobbins for New England textile factories, burned in 1889 and rebuilt larger, expecting to employ 100 to 200 hands.

sources.quote: In the summer of 1888 the first shop for the manufacture of rough bobbins, in the eastern part of this state, was established at Black Falls, so called, in this town
will employ from 100 to 200 hands

timeline.title: Fuller Bridge, the last Jewett bridge
timeline.text: The Jewetts completed the Fuller (Black Falls) Bridge north of the village, probably their last; the same year the Samson family's ownership of the village hotel ended.

sources.quote: they completed the Fuller Bridge in 1890, probably the last of their bridge projects.
Various members of the Samson (also spelled Sampson) family owned the inn until 1890.

timeline.title: Population peaks at 1,876
timeline.text: The census of 1900 recorded the most people Montgomery has ever had; it then fell for seventy years to 651 in 1970.

sources.quote: Montgomery’s population reached it’s apex in 1900 with 1,876 people, making it the 6th largest town of the 15 in Franklin County.

timeline.title: Butter-tub output at its height
timeline.text: The Nelson and Hall mill on the Hazen's Notch road (Route 58) was turning out about 800,000 tubs a year, matching the Hutchins mill south of Montgomery Center, which had employed about 150 men at that rate in the late 1890s.

sources.quote: In 1906 production had risen to 800,000 tubs/yr.
The Hutchins mill, shown above, had 150 men making 800,000/yr.

timeline.title: Maple sugar, and the last fire at the Hutchins mill
timeline.text: Montgomery made 179,000 lb of maple sugar, the most of any Franklin County town, and the big Hutchins tub mill burned for the final time.

sources.quote: In 1914 Montgomery produced 179,000 pounds of Maple Sugar.
In 1914 Montgomery was the largest producer of maple sugar (not syrup) in Franklin County.

timeline.title: Flood of November 1927
timeline.text: The statewide flood of 3-4 November 1927 struck Montgomery; local accounts and a state map of road damage suggest it was less severe there than the 1997 flood.

sources.quote: The summer of 1976 brought the worst flooding since November 3-4, 1927 to Montgomery.

timeline.text: Jay Peak, Inc., formed around April 1955 with backing from the North Troy Kiwanis Club, started its first lift in January 1957 after six towns including Montgomery agreed in 1956 to fund a road to the mountain.

timeline.title: The Jay Road links Montgomery to Jay Peak
timeline.text: A ribbon was cut in June 1957 on the new section of the Jay Road, giving direct travel from Montgomery to Jay Peak and Jay; which the National Register form credits with keeping the village inn in business.

timeline.title: Montgomery's covered bridges listed on the National Register
timeline.text: Nominated together by the Vermont Division of Historic Sites, the six Montgomery bridges and the Hopkins Bridge were listed between 19 November and 31 December 1974, recognised as the largest surviving body of work by any Vermont covered-bridge builders.

sources.quote: the Montgomery bridges constitute the most extensive surviving record of the work of any individual covered bridge builders who practiced their trade in Vermont.

sources.quote: They normally were named for the family, area, structure, or geographic feature nearby. Over time a bridge could have two or three names.

bridge_context.claim: 'Covered Bridge Capital': there were 11 to 13 covered bridges in the town at their height (11 around 1945); six stand within the town and one straddles the Enosburg line.

sources.quote: Montgomery is known as Vermont’s Covered Bridge Capital.
Depending who you talk to there were between 11-13 covered bridges at one point in time.
giving it the highest concentration of covered bridges by town in Vermont.

bridge_context.claim: Why so many bridges: they carried logs to the mills and butter tubs and lumber out, especially to the rail transshipment point at East Berkshire.

sources.quote: This reflects an abundance of raw materials, water power, and a rail transshipment point nearby in E. Berkshire for easy shipment of finished goods.

place_names.name: West Hill / Hill West Road
place_names.origin: West Hill is one of the hill districts the town has long been divided into (North, East and West Hills). West Hill Road and Hill West Road are separate roads; the Jewett brothers lived and milled in the 'Hill West / West Hill area'.

sources.quote: The terms North, East, and West Hills, and Notch road are respectively used to designate certain hilly and geographical portions of the town.
West Hill Rd and Hill West Rd are different roads!
They came from a large family and lived mostly in the Hill West / West Hill area.

place_names.name: Collar Hill
place_names.origin: Named after a short-lived early settler called Collar, who cleared a little land there in the 1790s and left.

sources.quote: known from this beginning, by the soubriquet of " Collar Hill " to this day.

place_names.name: Black Falls
place_names.origin: A falls and mill site on Black Falls Brook north of the village; site of the 1888 bobbin factory. Three miles from the inn, according to its c.1915 advertisement.

sources.quote: One-half mile to Gates' Falls, three miles to Black Falls.

economy_2004.claim: Jay Peak's owner in 2004 was Mont Saint-Sauveur International (MSSI) of Quebec, which bought the resort in 1978 and sold it in 2008. MSSI had tried to sell from 1996, citing lack of capital, and a 1997 deal fell through in January 1998.

sources.quote: The owners of Mont Saint Sauveur acquired Jay Peak from Weyerhaeuser Co. in 1978.
In September 1996, MSSI announced its intention to sell Jay Peak, stating a lack of capital for needed investments.
Mont Saint Sauver International (MSSI), an owner and operator of Canadian-based ski resorts, had owned the Resort since 1978.

economy_2004.claim: Jay Peak's workforce around 2004: about 100 full-time, year-round jobs before the 2005 expansion, rising to 550 in winter and 100 in summer by 2006. It was a seasonal employer, not a year-round one.

sources.quote: The mountain provided only 100 full-time, year-round jobs, and few more seasonal opportunities.
sources.note: Ski Magazine, 2 August 2010, describing the period before 2005.

sources.quote: In 2006, the resort employed 550 people in the winter, 100 in the summer.
sources.note: Wikipedia cites the Chronicle (Barton), 29 August 2007.

economy_2004.claim: Census Bureau ZIP Code Business Patterns for March 2004 show how small the payroll economy of Montgomery itself was: Montgomery village (05470) had 6 establishments with 37 employees and Montgomery Center (05471) had 22 with 119. Accommodation and food services was the largest sector by establishments in Montgomery Center (5 of 22), followed by retail and real estate (4 each). The figures exclude farms, the self-employed and government.

sources.note: Fields: zip, name, empflag, employees (mid-March 2004), Q1 payroll $1000, annual payroll $1000, establishments.
NAICS 72 (accommodation and food services): 5 establishments by employee-size class.

economy_2004.claim: The largest workplace near Montgomery was over the mountain: ZIP 05859 (North Troy, which includes Jay) had 564 employees in March 2004, and one hotel/motel establishment (NAICS 721110) in the 250-499 employee class, the only workplace of that size in the Montgomery, Montgomery Center, Enosburg Falls, Richford or North Troy ZIPs. The Census does not name establishments; that it is Jay Peak Resort is an inference.

Nearby service and factory towns in March 2004: Enosburg Falls (05450) had 99 establishments and 936 employees, including a cheese plant with 50-99 workers; Richford (05476) had 45 establishments and 450 employees. St. Albans (05478), the county seat, had 499 establishments and 6,726 employees. Its largest were a general hospital (500-999 employees) and a pharmaceutical plant (250-499), with an ice-cream plant among several factories of 100-249. The source names no employers.

sources.note: NAICS 311513 = cheese manufacturing.
NAICS 622110 = general medical and surgical hospitals.
NAICS 325412 = pharmaceutical preparation manufacturing.
NAICS 311520 = ice cream and frozen dessert manufacturing.

economy_2004.claim: Dairy: Franklin County was Vermont's leading dairy county, with the state's largest cattle herd (62,700 head) and an estimated 38,800 milk cows on 1 January 2002. Orleans County, which includes Jay, was third with 24,100 milk cows.

sources.quote: Franklin County continued to have the largest cattle and calf inventory in Vermont with 62,700 head
Franklin County had an estimated 38,800 milk cows, followed by Addison County with 32,700 and Orleans County with 24,100.

economy_2004.claim: Tourism: Montgomery's economy is described as centred on tourism because of Jay Peak, with agriculture second. The 1991 Register form credits the 1957 Jay Peak road with keeping the village inn in business. The current town plan notes that Jay Peak staff often live in or near Montgomery. These are undated or later descriptions, not 2004 measurements.

sources.quote: Montgomery's economy centers on tourism due to its proximity to Jay Peak Resort. Agribusiness is also a significant contributor to the town's economy.
The Montgomery House has been able to remain a viable commercial enterprise during more recent years
Although located in Jay, the Jay Peak Ski Area brings in more potential tourists to their town and its bordering neighbors like Montgomery.
many of whom reside in or around Montgomery.
sources.note: Of Jay Peak staff.

economy_2004.claim: Transport in 2004: there was no railway. The Missisquoi branch through East Berkshire had been abandoned in 1990-92 and became a rail trail in 1994-95. VT-118 (to Berkshire and Enosburg), VT-58 (over Hazen's Notch) and VT-242 (to Jay Peak) meet at Montgomery Center.

sources.quote: Limited operations continued on either side of the river, until the western section was abandoned in 1990 and the eastern in 1992.
Vermont Route 242 also terminates at Montgomery Center, leading northeast over the Green Mountains to Jay.

inn.claim: Built about 1803 as a brick Federal-style village hotel with a twin-gabled front, 'probably unique in the state' for its type; the National Register lists it as the Montgomery House.

sources.quote: The Montgomery House, built c.1803 and located in the center of the village of Montgomery, Vermont, is a well-preserved example of a 21/2 story, brick, twin gable front, Federal style hotel with later changes.
The Montgomery House is reputed to have been built in 1803, one of the earliest buildings in the town still in existence.

inn.claim: Former names: Samson's Hotel, Mansfield House (c.1915), Laplant House (c.1915-1922) and Black Lantern Inn. The inn's own 2003 website spelled it 'Sampson'.

sources.quote: Various members of the Samson (also spelled Sampson) family owned the inn until 1890.
It was known as the "Laplant House" (c.1915-1922) and had a succession of other names as it passed through a series of owners.
Accordingly, an advertisement for the Mansfield House, with S.M. Coan, Proprietor, (as the Montgomery House was known c. 1915)

inn.claim: Owned by the Samson family from at least 1857 to 1890. In 1883 Aaron S. Samson ran it while also serving as deputy sheriff and register of probate.

sources.quote: In 1857, the hotel belonged to Tolman Samson1 , who is documented as having a son born in Montgomery in 1814 and who appears to be the earliest documented owner.
sources.note: Footnote 1 cites H. F. Walling, Survey Map of Franklin and Grand Isle Counties, 1857.

sources.quote: SAMSON AARON S., (Montgomery) r 8, deputy sheriff, register of probate, prop. Montgomery House, and farmer about 35.
sources.note: Hamilton Child's 1882-83 business directory.

inn.claim: The stagecoach-era road: the hotel stood on the 'Boston and Montreal Turnpike', and the Register form says early-19th-century taverns clustered at stage-route junctions. The inn's own 2003 website called it a stagecoach inn; the Register form doesn't say that stages stopped at this house.

sources.quote: Tourism in Vermont during the early part of the 19th century was dependent upon stage roads and most taverns were located at important stage route junctions along the most passable roads.
Montgomery House was ideally located on the "Boston and Montreal Turnpike", thereby deriving benefit from the public recognition and maintenance of the highway.

inn.claim: The inn was the village's first civic centre: with no public building until the churches of the 1830s and 1840s, it hosted public gatherings, travellers and salesmen ('drummers') on the road to Montreal.

sources.quote: With the lack of a public building in Montgomery, the Montgomery House was of necessity the focal point for any kind of public activity as well as a place to obtain food, drink and sleeping accommodations.
The location of Montgomery along the old military road through Hazen's Notch that later became a market route to Montreal provided travelling businessmen4 and the era's early tourists.

inn.claim: Railway-era resort trade: a wood-framed rear wing was added about 1860. In about 1915 the Mansfield House advertised itself to anglers and cyclists as five miles from the East Berkshire station, with board at $1-2 a day.

sources.quote: Evidence of business expansion accompanying this era is the wood-framed rear wing that was added to the original brick block of the Montgomery House c.1860.
Five miles from East Berkshire C.V.R. station.

inn.claim: Ski era: the Register form credits the 1957 road to Jay Peak with keeping the hotel in business as the Black Lantern Inn. It was nominated in 1991 and listed on 20 August 1992 (ref. 92000997).

sources.quote: currently doing hotel business as the Black Lantern Inn, due to the opening of the road to Jay Peak in 1957 from Montgomery
It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1992.

inn.claim: The town plan today counts the Black Lantern among the village's landmarks, with Pratt Hall (the former St. Bartholomew's Episcopal Church, 1835) and the Baptist church.

sources.quote: historic landmarks such as the Black Lantern, Pratt Hall, and the Baptist Church.
This building was Montgomery’s first church, completed in 1835, and is home to our Historical Society.

Context only. Nothing here concerns any person, family or business connected with the 2004 case, and none is implied. The surnames on bridges and roads are 19th-century names, and no source ties them to anyone living. No property or parcel records were consulted. One flood-buyout address in the 2017 hazard plan was deliberately left out.

Quotes from the 19th-century books (Hemenway 1871, Child 1883, Aldrich 1891) come from the Internet Archive OCR text, with whitespace normalised and line-end hyphens rejoined. OCR slips are flagged where they appear in a quote.
Wikipedia quotes were taken from page wikitext (action=raw) with the markup stripped. Wikipedia was read as a secondary source and checked against NRHP forms wherever possible.

Grading: 'primary' covers NRHP nomination forms, the charter text, federal and state data (Census, USDA NASS, NWS), the 1883 business directory and the town's own plans. Town histories, newspapers, ski-history sites and the Historical Society's compilations are 'secondary'.

ZIP Code Business Patterns describe ZIP areas, not towns, for the pay period including 12 March 2004. They exclude farm workers, the self-employed and most government employment, and give single establishments only as size classes, without names. Identifying the 250-499 hotel in ZIP 05859 as Jay Peak is an inference.

There are no economy figures for Montgomery for 2004 itself beyond the ZIP data. The Vermont Department of Labor's 2004 Economic-Demographic Profile (vtlmi) returned HTTP 503, and the Census API now requires a key.
Bridge coordinates come from the NRIS-derived Wikipedia infoboxes (WGS84, rounded). The Hectorville position is the former Gibou Road site; the bridge was in storage in 2004.

archive.org was reachable from this machine during this run, despite the brief, so the djvu.txt texts were fetched and used directly. web.archive.org was not tried. Wikimedia's API rate-limited this machine (HTTP 429), so Commons was read through ordinary file and category pages.
The Wild and Scenic designation (2014) is outside the 1779-2004 span and was left out except as context in the Historical Society's bridge history.

not_verified.tried: NRHP 1991 form (NPGallery and the Historical Society copy) and the 1883 and 1891 county histories. The form places the hotel on the 'Boston and Montreal Turnpike' and says taverns sat at stage-route junctions, but no source states that stagecoaches stopped here or dates the turnpike.

not_verified.claim: That FEMA's help to buy Riverwalk Park followed the 1997 flood. One secondary source says so (the Wild and Scenic committee). The town's 2017 hazard plan records a 2010 flood buyout of a different property, a house on West Hill Road, and does not mention the park.
not_verified.tried: NWS 1997 report, 2017 Local Hazard Mitigation Plan, 2024 Town Plan, Historical Society newsletters, web search. The town plan names a 'River Walk Park' and a Riverwalk Community Garden (2010), and the hazard plan records a FEMA-type residential buyout completed in 2010. No source links a 1997 buyout to the park.

The charter text transcribed by the Historical Society says 15 March 1780 (as does Wikipedia). Child (1883), Hemenway (1871), Aldrich (1891) and the 2024 town plan say 13 March. Unresolved without the original State Papers volume.

not_verified.claim: Origins of the names Comstock, Longley (aka Harnois, Head), Fuller and Hopkins.
not_verified.tried: All seven NRHP forms, the Historical Society's bridge history and pamphlet, VCBS, Wikipedia, Child (1883) and Aldrich (1891). The county histories list 19th-century residents with these surnames, but none ties a surname to a bridge.

not_verified.claim: Build years of the Hectorville and West Hill (Creamery) bridges.
not_verified.tried: The 1974 NRHP forms say 'unknown'. The 2024 town plan and the Historical Society's pamphlet give 1883. The Hectorville Wikipedia infobox gives 1860.

not_verified.claim: When the Hectorville bridge was moved from the village to Hectorville.
not_verified.tried: Wikipedia says 'early 1900s'. A search snippet credited to the Historical Society gave 1899, but the page carrying it was not found. The Society's bridge history suggests it may first have spanned the village 'gutter'.

not_verified.claim: The second Jewett brother's first name.

Wikipedia's census table gives 41. The Historical Society's population PDF gives 36 in one table and 34 in the other, and its timeline gives 34. Page 27 of the 1800 federal return (census.gov) appears to give Vermont by county only.

not_verified.claim: Date of Weyerhaeuser's investment in Jay Peak.
not_verified.tried: NESH says shareholders agreed in January (1966) to sell shares to Weyerhaeuser; Wikipedia says 1968.

No exact date was found for the arrival at East Berkshire or Richford. Wikipedia says only 'built during the 1870s'.
