years.label: Roommate finds the note undisturbed
years.detail: The roommate returns and finds the note where it was left. Roommate and parents each assumed she was with the other.

years.label: Reported missing
years.detail: She is reported missing on Tuesday 23 March, four days after her shift.

years.label: BCI takes over as a major case
years.detail: VSP's Bureau of Criminal Investigation takes over on 25 March and runs it as a major case. Police show her mother photos of the car about then.

years.label: VSP search with K-9 and helicopter
years.detail: K-9 and a National Guard helicopter search the scene: loose change, a water bottle, an unsmoked cigarette, and an item of interest later sent for DNA (none of those three).

years.label: First TV report
years.detail: WPTZ's first report: police are searching. Her parents say she left her belongings, including her driver's license, at the friend's house.

years.label: Father finds a woman's fleece jacket
years.detail: After the police search, her father finds a woman's size-small fleece jacket near the scene, its wallet full of Canadian money and another woman's cards. Its owner was later found; unconnected.

years.label: Police: not calling it suspicious
years.detail: AP: police are not calling her disappearance suspicious. Her mother told the Messenger: 'That was no accident.' A coworker reportedly said she talked of a short trip.

years.label: State crime lab processes the car
years.detail: After several days at a local garage the car is processed by the state crime lab. Lt. Nelson: 'nothing concrete as to her whereabouts'.

years.label: Nelson: 'not a regular accident'
years.detail: Lt. Nelson: the car looked backed into the building, not a regular accident; no sign of a violent struggle; the ground between the scene and the inn not yet searched.

years.label: KlaasKids volunteer search
years.detail: From Montgomery Town Hall: about 300 searchers Friday-Saturday and 100 Sunday (AP), high ground first, the Trout River by kayak. Ended early under 4-6 in. of new snow.

years.label: Gable re-boarded, flowers tied on
years.detail: A dated private-investigator photo shows the hole the car punched in the west gable already covered with fresh plywood, flowers tied on. Who repaired it is not recorded.

years.label: Searchers find T-shirt, knife, taped item
years.detail: WPTZ: searchers found a purple T-shirt, a knife and a large spoon near the car, and tape with hair stuck to it. Nelson said nothing found was connected.

years.label: Family's roadside search
years.detail: A family search covers about 30 miles of roadside in Richford, Berkshire, Enosburg and Montgomery; lost clothing found, none hers.

years.label: Police raid a Berkshire house
years.detail: On an anonymous tip that she was held there, police raid a Berkshire house rented by two men described as New York drug dealers. Drugs and guns found; no sign of her.

years.label: Father criticizes state police
years.detail: Her father writes to the governor criticising VSP's slow start: the scene photos show snow and unreadable footprints, melted before anyone knew she was missing.

years.label: Family offers $10,000
years.detail: The family offers a $10,000 award for her return and launches bringbrihome.org.

years.label: Family meets VSP's chief investigators
years.detail: After the father's letter, the family meets VSP's chief criminal investigators; police promise better communication and weekly meetings follow.

years.label: Forensic work along the river
years.detail: WPTZ: police are doing forensic evaluations along the river behind the barn, the Trout River about 220 m behind the house. What prompted it is not public.

years.label: Joint appeal with Maura Murray's family
years.detail: In Haverhill, NH, her parents, Maura Murray's father and another missing woman's parents appeal for FBI help.

years.label: PI firm reports finds near scene
years.detail: A private investigation firm says it found women's underwear of her size under cut brush, three cut flex-cuffs with hair, and a blue syringe, and gave them to VSP. Testing is not public.

years.label: WPTZ editorial urges FBI help
years.detail: WPTZ's on-air editorial says both states should call in the FBI.

years.label: Petition drive and father's letter
years.detail: A Franklin grandmother circulates petitions demanding state action; her father's letter to papers says 'Brianna is not a runaway'.

years.label: Mother's op-ed: not a runaway
years.detail: Her mother's op-ed in the Burlington Free Press, titled in a secondary index 'My daughter is not a runaway; Brianna was abducted'.

years.label: FBI Quantico unit reviews the case
years.detail: FBI behavioral scientists from Quantico review VSP's work on this case and Maura Murray's; the FBI says it has worked with VSP nearly from the start.

years.label: VSP, NHSP and FBI meet
years.detail: Joint meeting in St. Albans: 61 people interviewed, seven subpoenaed before a judge, one search warrant. 'There is no serial killer on the loose in the area.'

years.label: Parents meet Lt. Governor
years.detail: Her parents meet Lt. Gov. Brian Dubie and the public-safety commissioner for two hours; the runaway listing is dropped.

years.label: VSP: foul play may be involved
years.detail: Press conference: VSP says foul play may be involved and two people said she owed money for drugs. A new flier photo's origin was unknown. Family reward stands at $10,000.

years.label: Police: no link to Murray case
years.detail: After four hours with the FBI, Vermont and New Hampshire investigators find 'no connection whatsoever'. They appeal: 'We don't care about' drug pasts. The family canoes the Missisquoi.

years.label: River camera search; manure pit pumped
years.detail: Her parents search deep holes in the Missisquoi with a borrowed underwater camera, choosing stretches ice-free in March. A Sheldon manure pit is pumped on tips; nothing found.

years.label: Six months on, 'no closer'
years.detail: Her father: 'we're no closer now than we were the first day or two.' WPTZ lists her pay stub, some money and her license as left in the car.

years.label: VSP releases the car to her parents
years.detail: VSP releases the car to her parents in late September. Her father later finds her ATM card, glasses, contact case and migraine medicine inside; keys never found.

years.label: PI firm says it found blood spots
years.detail: The PI firm processes the released car and says it found three blood spots under the driver's armrest (alternate light only), a syringe cap, green fibres and a shoe print.

years.label: Charley Project adds her case
years.detail: The Charley Project adds her case on 12 Oct 2004.

years.label: VSP lists her first among major cases
years.detail: By 14 Oct 2004 VSP's major-cases page lists her case first.

years.label: Volunteer's metal detector finds coins
years.detail: A volunteer searcher's metal detector finds coins where her driver's door would have opened, at a depth he judged consistent with the months since.

years.label: Joint family press conference
years.detail: The Maitland and Murray families schedule a joint press conference in Woodsville, NH.

years.label: Interview count reaches 107
years.detail: By December 2004 investigators had interviewed 107 people; the subpoenaed witnesses appeared at an inquest.

years.label: America's Most Wanted airs the case
years.detail: AMW airs the case (also 3 Sep 2005 and 18 Mar 2006). Its January 2005 case file has the 1:22 am trooper line.

years.label: Agencies meet; memorial walk
years.detail: Investigators from several agencies and the FBI meet on 18 March; a memorial walk of her route from the inn to the house starts 11:20 am on the 19th.

years.label: Volunteer inspects the car
years.detail: A volunteer sits in the car: power seat still set for her size, fuel in the tank, necklace on the passenger seat, DNA cuts in the rear seat, no blood; gouged fuel tank underneath.

years.label: Divers and dogs search Berkshire
years.detail: VSP divers and Connecticut scent dogs search woods, wetland and a pond in Berkshire; about 25 officers; nothing found and no new information prompted it.

years.label: Raid man arrested in New York
years.detail: One of the April 2004 raid men is arrested in New York City; his plea required cooperation in the investigation, not specific information.

years.label: EquuSearch asked not to come
years.detail: Reported: police asked Texas EquuSearch not to come, citing new leads, after a convicted drug dealer agreed to give information.

years.label: The car is junked
years.detail: After its release her father junked the car, by one account in September 2005. Gear, seat and fuel can now come only from records.

years.label: Cadaver-dog search, Montgomery and Berkshire
years.detail: Two-day VSP search with teams from several states: 44 people and 17 dogs. Police said the coming snow, not new information, prompted it. Family reward: up to $20,000.

years.label: Montgomery double homicide, unrelated
years.detail: Two adults are found dead on VT-242 in Montgomery; two Connecticut residents are arrested within days for a robbery. Nobody linked it to her.

years.label: Casino camera films a lookalike
years.detail: Caesars Atlantic City cameras film a lookalike at a blackjack table (monitor stamp 01-17-06 03:55:30). A man from near her home town calls VSP on 19 January. Judged not her.

years.label: Affidavit alleges a killing over money
years.detail: A notarized statement, after a March 2006 arrest, alleges a drug dealer killed her about a week after she vanished. Never corroborated; its supposed source denied it.

years.label: Casino video made public
years.detail: AP and the Messenger report the casino video. Her father warns supporters not to get excited; family members split on whether it is her.

years.label: WND: trooper on patrol spotted car
years.detail: WorldNetDaily reports the car was first noticed by a trooper on regular patrol, less than 12 hours after she vanished.

years.label: Glenn Hall takes over the case
years.detail: Acting Capt. Glenn Hall of VSP takes over the case in fall 2006; he leads it publicly for years.

years.label: FBI flyer: scene may be staged
years.detail: An FBI flyer says the scene may have been staged to look like an accident.

years.label: Affidavit story published
years.detail: The County Courier publishes the affidavit; her parents had learned of it only in late January. VSP had known since March 2006.

years.label: Hall: leads suggest she is not alive
years.detail: Det. Lt. Glenn Hall: some leads indicate she is not alive, unverified; most information is second-hand. Friends hold a vigil in Enosburg Falls.

years.label: VSP starts expanded review
years.detail: From May 2007 VSP dedicates detectives to an expanded review and re-interviews many people.

years.label: NBC News feature
years.detail: NBC News: the paychecks totalled under $150; Det. Miller saw no sign of a struggle; her parents already held the back-seat stowaway theory.

years.label: Detectives return to Atlantic City
years.detail: Two detectives return to Atlantic City to check a second sighting reported by a business owner.

years.label: Women's jeans found off Gibou Road
years.detail: A man finds weathered women's jeans in woods off Gibou Road, Montgomery, about 4-7 miles from the inn. Searches find no remains; a hair goes to the FBI lab.

years.label: Mile-square search around the jeans
years.detail: VSP Search and Rescue, four Connecticut K-9 units and New England K-9 SAR search a mile-square area not searched before.

years.label: Jeans tested: not hers
years.detail: The 2007 jeans were tested for DNA and were not hers. VSP says the early drug-activity link could not be substantiated, attributed largely to rumours.

years.label: VSP changes missing-person procedures
years.detail: VSP announces new missing-person report procedures, crediting a year of talks with her father. Later every missing person's family gets a trooper liaison.

years.label: NamUs record MP2030 created
years.detail: Her NamUs missing-person record MP2030 is created; its three photos date from that day.

years.label: Search at the scene with game wardens
years.detail: VSP and Fish & Wildlife wardens search the fields, woods and riverbank near where the car was found, following leads.

years.label: K-9 search near Prive Hill Road
years.detail: VSP Search and Rescue with a K-9 searches the Prive Hill Road area of Richford, a search planned for some time; nothing found.

years.label: VSP offers up to $5,000
years.detail: VSP begins offering up to $5,000, from seized cash, in 40 major cases including hers. Its case page still shows this figure.

years.label: FBI wanted poster record published
years.detail: The FBI's current Kidnappings and Missing Persons poster record is published (last modified 2026).

years.label: Disappeared: 'Vanished in Vermont' airs
years.detail: Investigation Discovery's Disappeared (S4E11) airs with Glenn Hall and family. Rewards: $20,000 from the family, up to $5,000 from VSP.

years.label: Israel Keyes ruled out
years.detail: The FBI examines serial killer Israel Keyes and rules him out; financial records placed him outside Vermont.

years.label: Danby skull: possible match named
years.detail: VSP names her as a possible match for a young woman's skull found in Danby; investigators had her DNA on file. No identification followed.

years.label: 10th anniversary vigil at the farmhouse
years.detail: Friends hold a candlelight vigil at the farmhouse. Vermont's intelligence center starts a missing-persons Facebook page with her flyer.

years.label: Lab matches car DNA to people she knew
years.detail: A state lab report, cited in the PI's book, matches one car sample to an ex-boyfriend and others to close friends; a print matched a friend.

years.label: The Black Lantern Inn closes
years.detail: The Black Lantern Inn closed in 2015; it was closed by February 2016.

years.label: VSP: DNA from her car
years.detail: VSP says DNA evidence from her car could shed new light; it won't say when it was found. VSP launches its unsolved-case web pages with her case.

years.label: The Dutchburn house burns down
years.detail: The abandoned house where her car was found burns to the ground. The PIs think kids set it and were caught. Aerials show it gone by 2016-20.

years.label: Det. Sgt. Angela Baker takes the case
years.detail: Det. Sgt. Angela Baker becomes the case officer, about January 2017 by her own account.

years.label: Podcast: PI recalls travellers' time
years.detail: On Missing Maura Murray eps 37-38, the investigator who processed the car puts the travellers at 'around 10, 11 o'clock' and describes his firm's finds.

years.label: 'Bring Bri Home' tip day
years.detail: A non-profit runs a one-day tip campaign at a St. Albans hotel; it reports several promising leads. The family's $20,000 reward is set to expire 1 July 2017.

years.label: Family reward expires
years.detail: The family's $20,000 reward ($10,000 for her location, $10,000 for an arrest) expires.

years.label: Father starts nonprofit for the missing
years.detail: Her father starts a nonprofit to help families of missing people; his PIs work with police. Hall: the case changed how VSP handles missing persons.

years.label: Maj. Glenn Hall retires
years.detail: Maj. Glenn Hall, a lead on the case since 2006, retires.

years.label: PIs and father's live show
years.detail: Live show in Nashua with her father and both PIs; the ex-boyfriend had contacted a PI weeks before. VSP and the lead PI say he was not involved.

years.label: Ex-boyfriend dies in a car crash
years.detail: The ex-boyfriend who shut the car's doors that night dies in a head-on crash. He was never accused; police and PIs said he was not involved.

years.label: VSP partners with Othram
years.detail: VSP partners with Othram for genetic genealogy on DNA from the K-9 search item; The Murder Squad funds the work.

years.label: Lead detective on The Murder Squad
years.detail: Det. Sgt. Baker: one passer-by's disposable camera documented the scene; police took about one photo; very few knew where she worked; no evidence she ran away.

years.label: House's address point deleted
years.detail: The house's E911 address point is deleted between the February and October 2021 snapshots, dating the site's clearance.

years.label: DNA source identified, not involved
years.detail: The K-9 item's DNA is traced to a man with no involvement who gave a voluntary sample in 2004. It matched none of 11 persons of interest.

years.label: Records request denied
years.detail: A public-records request for the case file is closed 'Not Fulfilled, Statutory Exemption'; another in January 2026 meets the same answer.

years.label: PI publishes 'The Hunt for Brianna Maitland'
years.detail: PI Greg Overacker, with the family since 2006, publishes his book and discusses it on the Missing podcast.

years.label: FBI and VSP offer $40,000
years.detail: On the 20th anniversary the FBI and VSP offer up to $40,000 for information leading to her recovery, the first government reward. The FBI will help digitise the files.

years.label: More items sent for DNA testing
years.detail: Det. Sgt. Baker: VSP sent 'a bunch of other items' back to the lab for new DNA testing, with about 18 boxes of files.

years.label: Dark Downeast episode with Barry
years.detail: PI Lou Barry narrates the scene and the overnight accounts on Dark Downeast; source of several audit corrections.

years.label: New witnesses revealed
years.detail: At a fundraiser recording the PIs reveal the couple's account of the man and the silver Civic; they came forward after the 2024 reward.

years.label: PI Lou Barry dies
years.detail: PI Lou Barry, a retired police chief who worked the case for the family from 2016, dies; the Missing podcast airs a tribute episode.

years.label: Appeal for a grey or silver Civic
years.detail: Missing ep. 26 airs and the PIs post 'Do you recognize this vehicle?', seeking a grey or silver 1990s-2000 Civic on VT-118 around 11:30-11:45 pm.

years.label: A traveller posts his memories
years.detail: A man saying he was one of the three travellers posts on Reddit: the barn fire, friends climbing into the house, statements to VSP.

years.label: 22nd anniversary
years.detail: Her father continues the search; many tips over the years were false. A former lead says today's technology would have produced many more leads.

years.label: She would turn 40
years.detail: Born 8 Oct 1986, she turns 40. Still a missing person; no remains found.

top_story.label: Someone she knew stopped her and took her

items.label: Quebec biker war: duration and toll
items.detail: Ran July 1994 to June 2002 with 160+ killed (165 dead and 200+ wounded in one tally). A truce brokered by the Rizzuto family after the September 2000 shooting of journalist Michel Auger lasted weeks. Boucher convicted May 2002. The Bandidos/Rock Machine had ceded Quebec to the Hells Angels by 2003.

items.label: Court confiscates Sherbrooke Hells Angels compound used during the drug war
items.detail: 2017 Superior Court decision covering 1994–2002, when the Hells 'waged a drug war to expand its reach'. In 2012, 24 Sherbrooke chapter members pleaded guilty to conspiring to kill rivals and independent dealers who refused to buy from the Hells.

items.label: Opération Cisaille: SQ's yearly farmland cannabis eradication, started 1999
items.detail: Snippets: launched 1999 after organised crime moved into cornfields and forests. In 2009, 694,630 plants were seized province-wide, about 200,000 of them in Montérégie. I found no 2001–2006 annual totals.

items.label: Sutton-based smuggling and money-laundering organisation
items.detail: A Sutton, Quebec man led a group moving Canadian marijuana into the US and cash back north from 1998 until his July 2002 arrest. He fought extradition for about 8 years and was sentenced to 168 months in Vermont federal court in 2011.

items.label: Drug crimes +27% 1997–2000; federal heroin sentences surge
items.detail: Drug-only crimes rose from 2,052 to 2,608 while total crime fell. Federal heroin sentences went from 4 in FY1999 to 26 in FY2000.

items.label: Montgomery/Richford pair ran cross-border bulk marijuana importing (began mid-2000s)
items.detail: Search snippet only: two Franklin County men, one from Montgomery and one from Richford, called kingpins of a business that 'began in the mid-2000s' and brought bulk marijuana across the Canadian border into northern Vermont until their May 2013 arrests.

items.label: Montgomery-led ring: up to 3,000 kg from the mid-2000s to 2013
items.detail: 11 Vermont men near the border convicted; the leader, of Montgomery, was said to have brought in up to 3,000 kg from Quebec from the mid-2000s until 2013. $600,000 cash, over 70 guns, 17 vehicles and 3 properties seized. The judge said a Richford defendant was supporting dangerous gangs in Quebec. Methods not disclosed. Start date overlaps the end of the study window.

items.label: Rutland raid: courier claimed 20,000 bags from NYC Dominicans
items.detail: Raids in Bennington, Plainfield and Rutland seized more than 1,000 bags in Rutland. One arrestee said he had brought 20,000 bags in 7 months, bought from a Dominican group in New York City.

items.label: 'Quebec Gold' grown in cornfields south of Montreal, sold in New York
items.detail: Growers squat on farmers' land, fencing 'a long, thin strip of cornfield' with razor wire and using intimidation. Sold as 'Quebec Gold' on New York streets. Pre-2001 context.

items.place: Quebec (Montreal and ~75 municipalities); also Ontario, Alberta
items.label: Operation Springtime (Opération Printemps 2001): province-wide sweep against Hells Angels Nomads and Rockers
items.detail: About 2,000 officers in three provinces; most Nomads arrested. Maurice 'Mom' Boucher charged with 13 more counts of first-degree murder. Billed as the biggest police operation of its kind in Canadian history. Arrest counts in different sources range from about 120 to 138.

items.label: How the Hells Angels drug pyramid worked (bail-hearing evidence)
items.detail: Other Quebec chapters bought their drugs from the Nomads. The Sherbrooke chapter once bought 350 kg of cocaine and paid the $12M bill within three weeks. Puppet gangs used violence and kidnapping to give each chapter a local monopoly. Cash flowed to Nomads counting houses in Montreal, where police once found $5.6M.

items.label: Treatment admissions FY2000–FY2001
items.detail: Heroin 373 to 696 (+87%); cocaine 310 to 298; marijuana 1,223 to 1,366; meth 12 to 4. Heroin arrests 141 to 177 (2000–2001).

items.place: Canada → US (mainly Detroit/Port Huron, not Quebec)
items.label: Operation Mountain Express III: Canadian pseudoephedrine supplying Mexican-run US meth superlabs
items.detail: DEA, January 2002: 'In the last two years, the use of Canadian pseudoephedrine has become the norm rather than the exception' in West Coast labs. 30+ tons pseudoephedrine seized, 300+ arrests. Smuggling ran mainly through Michigan; I found no Quebec-specific route.

items.label: NDIC 2005: Canadian MDMA labs rising; Asian groups press European powder into tablets; Montreal is an entry point
items.detail: RCMP MDMA lab seizures: 6 (2000), 8 (2001), 11 (2002). Asian groups are significant producers 'particularly in eastern provinces'. European MDMA enters via Toronto, Vancouver and Montreal. MDMA made in or passing through Canada reaches New York City by vehicle. Typical loads were 40,000–50,000 tablets.

items.label: SQ study: only about 23 synthesis labs neutralised in Quebec in a decade, half of them superlabs
items.detail: 46 sites in 38 police files: 23 synthesis labs (10 superlabs, 10 medium labs, 1 kitchen lab) plus storage, tableting and ephedrine-extraction sites. 184 kg of production neutralised in 2000–2004 versus 432 kg in 2006–2010. No more than about 30 chemists, some caught repeatedly. Quebec makes pills, not crystal meth.

items.label: SQ full report: early-2000s labs mostly ecstasy-only superlabs; first 'kitchen lab' only in 2010
items.detail: In 2000–2004, 60% of sites (4 superlabs and 2 medium labs) made only ecstasy-type drugs. The first small 'kitchen' (home meth) lab was found in 2010, run by an American-born user. Interviewees were almost all from the outlaw-biker milieu.

items.label: NDIC 2002: drugs bought out of state by local white dealers
items.detail: Drugs are typically bought in Massachusetts, Connecticut and New York, mainly by local independent Caucasian dealers, from Dominican groups. New York City is the primary regional distribution centre. Dominican groups that ran wholesale distribution in VT in the late 1990s moved away because they could not blend in.

items.label: NDIC 2002: I-89/I-91/I-93, St. Albans train, cheap NYC flights
items.detail: I-89 ends at the Highgate Springs port of entry and links to Montreal via Route 133 and Autoroutes 35/10. I-91 and I-93 connect to I-95. Named risks are the daily St. Albans–Washington train (with a New York City stop) and $49 Burlington–LaGuardia flights.

items.label: NDIC 2002: heroin from Dominican groups in MA/CT/NYC
items.detail: Local white retailers drive to Holyoke, Lawrence, Lowell, Springfield, Hartford and NYC. They buy at $7–10 a bag and resell at $20–45. Car traps typically hold 300–500 bags. Hispanic and white groups from NYC and MA occasionally sell wholesale from motels for a few days.

items.label: NDIC 2002: heroin not tied to violent crime
items.detail: Officials said heroin distribution was not commonly linked to violence, only to burglaries and robberies by users. Heroin investigations rose 372% (32 to 151) and heroin arrests 147% (57 to 141) from 1999 to 2000.

items.label: NDIC 2002: crack retailed by out-of-state African American groups
items.detail: Groups based in MA, CT and NY buy from Dominican suppliers, sell quickly in VT and go home, and increasingly cook crack in-state. A 2.5 kg Dominican supplier in MA was arrested alongside a VT dealer in Nov 2000.

items.label: NDIC 2002: OxyContin rising; MDMA via Montreal raves
items.detail: OxyContin abuse and pharmacy burglaries were rising (Rutland, Brattleboro, Newport). There were no raves in VT, but Burlington-area residents travelled to Montreal raves. MDMA sold in bars and homes.

items.label: NDIC 2002: no meth labs since 1990
items.detail: Meth threat low, averaging about 12 treatment admissions a year. The only significant seizure was 2 kg from California in 1999.

items.label: NDIC: Canadian marijuana backpacked through woods into Vermont
items.detail: DEA Burlington: Canadian marijuana increasingly available; some is driven to border areas in Canada, backpacked through the woods into Vermont while the empty vehicles cross at the port, then reloaded and driven to Vermont and other New England states. Some enters via Indian reservation land on the NY-Canada border. Occasionally through ports of entry.

items.label: Reservation-based cocaine ring leader sentenced (about 16 years)
items.detail: A 27-year-old man who smuggled cocaine from Canada onto the reservation and supplied local dealers was sentenced in Feb 2002 (arrested June 1999). NDIC: cocaine from Canada moves by private vehicle through the isolated part of the reservation; most seizures are personal-use amounts.

items.place: Highgate Springs VT port of entry
items.label: About 40 lb in a Canadian company's tractor-trailer
items.detail: An April 2002 interception (described in a 2005 court opinion) led ICE to put a lookout on all trucks of that Canadian trucking firm.

items.label: Franklin youths: OxyContin 80s at $100 a pill
items.detail: A St. Albans pediatrician found a BFA student had snorted four 80 mg tablets a day for 4 years before May 2006. Patients' drug of choice was OC 80s at $100 each; habits were funded by thefts across Swanton and St. Albans.

items.label: No evidence found of NY-vs-Quebec turf war
items.detail: Searches of NDIC, the US Attorney, the Senate hearing record and the Herald/Times Argus 2002–06 archives found no documented conflict between New York-based and Montreal-sourced suppliers. The only 'turf war' found was the 2001–02 Rutland crack dispute.

items.label: Project Amigos removes the Bandidos (ex-Rock Machine) from Quebec
items.detail: CISC: the operation ended in June 2002 with most Quebec Bandidos arrested, 'virtually eliminating the criminal influence of this group' in Quebec and Ontario. Wikipedia: 63 arrested; in 2003 the Bandidos agreed to leave Quebec.

items.label: About 45,000 Quebec growers at risk of arrest in 2002 (capture-recapture estimate)
items.detail: Search snippet of an academic study attributed to Bouchard (2007, J. Quant. Criminology). More indoor than outdoor growers; hydroponic growers mostly avoid detection.

items.label: New drug task force chief: $5 Holyoke bag sells for $35
items.detail: The VSP Drug Task Force commander said seizures had grown from 10–20 bags in the late 1990s to 200–300 bags. VCIC said heroin rose from 9% of drug arrests in 1997 to 31% in 2001.

items.label: Gap after Springtime filled by chapters not hit in 2001
items.detail: No members of the Sherbrooke, Sorel or St-Basile-le-Grand chapters were arrested in 2001; those chapters stepped into the Nomads' role. Quebec full-patch membership went from 106 (2001) to 124 (2002). Trois-Rivières became the coordinating chapter.

items.label: Vermont ecstasy demand partly met at Montreal raves
items.detail: 'Burlington area residents ... reportedly attend raves held across the border in Montreal.' MDMA was a limited threat in Vermont in 2001–2002.

items.label: Agent strength roughly doubled after 9/11
items.detail: About 90 agents in Vermont in 2001 (Seven Days, 2015). TRAC: Swanton Sector staff 83 (FY2001), 86 (FY2002), 97-98 (FY2003), 149 (FY2004), 170 (FY2005).

items.label: First methadone clinic 2002; buprenorphine 2003–04
items.detail: The HowardCenter methadone clinic opened in October 2002 (previously patients were treated out of state). Office-based buprenorphine started late 2003 to early 2004, and BAART opened in the Northeast Kingdom in 2005.

items.label: Pine St. alley killing in botched cocaine robbery
items.detail: Elrehaine Whitely was shot during a plan to rob him of an ounce of cocaine. Five people were prosecuted; the shooter, a Burlington man, 24, got 25 years to life in June 2005.

items.place: St. Regis Mohawk Reservation (Akwesasne), Franklin/St. Lawrence Cos. NY
items.label: NDIC NY: Akwesasne (Snye) a primary entry point
items.detail: Reservation straddles the Quebec/Ontario-NY border with no checkpoints; most drugs pass through the isolated Snye area. Marijuana and cocaine mainly; also heroin and MDMA. Canadian marijuana moves by tractor-trailer, private vehicle and bus, mostly via the reservation. Canadian Hells Angels chapters said to control most marijuana smuggling into NY.

items.label: NDIC NY: Hells Angels control most Canada-NY marijuana smuggling
items.detail: Canadian marijuana enters NY in tractor-trailers, private vehicles and buses, usually via the St. Regis Mohawk Reservation. Members of Canadian Hells Angels chapters and associated groups control most of it.

items.label: Rutland becomes an in-state 'source city'
items.detail: The task force chief said Vermonters now drove to Rutland instead of Holyoke or Albany, and crack made up about 50% of statewide task force cases. Rutland police said most local dealers were from out of state.

items.place: Lowell VT (about 15 mi south of border); arrest on I-91 near Lyndonville
items.label: 250 lb 'Quebec Gold' dropped by helicopter onto a snowmobile trail
items.detail: Border Patrol and Vermont State Police seized 250 lb flown in from Canada and dropped onto a snowmobile trail. The recipient, a Montreal resident, was arrested on I-91 and was reportedly a member of an organized group smuggling 'Quebec Gold'.

items.label: Yonkers-linked cocaine/heroin ring; 'armed dealers' quote
items.detail: Eight of 18 suspects were arrested, half from out of state (several from Yonkers, NY), with guns seized. The public safety commissioner said organised, armed dealers were setting up drug houses and saw Vermont's laws as weak.

items.label: UVM students smuggle Quebec pot via the Long Trail
items.detail: A Lennoxville, Quebec student and classmates walked 8+ lb across near Richford for resale at UVM. Buyers robbed and beat him in a dorm, which exposed the operation.

items.label: NDIC 2003 update: drugs from NY/MA/CT; smaller amounts from Canada
items.detail: Drugs come mainly from metro areas in NY, MA and CT by car, bus, train, plane and parcel. Smaller amounts come from Canada on foot, by snowmobile or by ATV. Most is consumed in VT, not transshipped.

items.label: NDIC 2003: heroin bought from Dominicans; some from Montreal
items.detail: Local white dealers buy bagged heroin at $6–10 a bag from Dominican groups in Holyoke, Lawrence, Lowell, Springfield, Hartford and NYC. They also smuggle smaller amounts from Montreal by car and increasingly bodypack. Source-city dealers occasionally rent motel rooms and sell up to 1,000 bags.

items.label: NDIC 2003: cocaine 3–4x NYC price; crack cooked locally
items.detail: Powder sold for $80–100/g, against $20–30/g in NYC. Whites bring in powder in cars with hidden compartments; small amounts cross from Canada. Crack is mostly converted locally by African American independents and sold from apartments and motels. Cocaine arrests rose from 134 (2000) to 208 (2001).

items.label: NDIC 2003: Canadian marijuana, sometimes by Hells Angels
items.detail: Most marijuana is Mexican, via MA and NY. Higher-grade Canadian marijuana crosses on foot, by snowmobile or by ATV and is handed to drivers, and is occasionally smuggled by Hells Angels members. Federal seizures totalled 450.1 kg in 2002.

items.label: NDIC 2003: OxyContin, MDMA from NYC/Europe; meth low
items.detail: OxyContin was involved in 6 deaths in 2001 and Medicaid stopped funding it. MDMA mostly comes from NYC by car or parcel, some by parcel direct from Europe. No meth labs seized since 1990.

items.label: Users swing between OxyContin and heroin
items.detail: Rutland police said that after heroin busts OxyContin use booms, and the reverse; OxyContin was gaining a foothold as a heroin substitute.

items.label: CBP Today, 'Quebec Gold: the other Canadian marijuana'
items.detail: Snippet only: a pound wholesaled at about C$3,000–3,500 in Quebec and could fetch about C$5,600 in New York State and up to C$7,000 in California. An RCMP investigator called it product sold largely into the US.

items.label: NDIC 2003 update: couriers on foot, snowmobiles, ATVs
items.detail: Higher-quality Canadian marijuana smuggled by vehicle and by couriers on foot, snowmobile or ATV, then handed to drivers on the US side. Hells Angels members occasionally smuggle it, mainly in private vehicles. Federal seizures in Vermont in 2002: 450.1 kg. Burlington prices Q4 FY2002: Canadian $250/oz vs Mexican $120-200/oz. Most of Vermont's marijuana was still Mexican, coming from MA and NY.

items.label: NDIC: Vermont ecstasy came from New York City, not Canada (2002)
items.detail: MDMA a 'low but growing threat'; generally transported from New York City by private vehicle or parcel service, sometimes from Europe by parcel. $18-30 per tablet (DEA Burlington, Q4 FY2002). Canada not named as a source.

items.label: Only documented 'turf war': NY crack dealer in Rutland
items.detail: A Hudson, NY man, 26, described as in a 'bitter turf war in Rutland with another drug dealer' (2001–02), took a 20-year plea. A charge that he arranged from jail for two New Yorkers to commit a murder was to be dismissed; an AK-47 and a TEC-9 were alleged.

items.label: DETER signed into law
items.detail: Drug Education, Treatment, Enforcement and Rehabilitation, signed June 2003. WAMC reported 'nearly $8 million'; the Herald reported $9.1M (June) and $3M (Oct). It included an 80-bed inpatient unit, school counsellors and tougher trafficking penalties.

items.label: CISC 2003: Quebec Hells Angels weakened; drugs remain main income
items.detail: 'Many of the six HELLS ANGELS chapters in this province lack the necessary active members and/or organizational capabilities.' Cocaine and marijuana trafficking is their primary income. Puppet clubs are declining. Two fugitive ex-Nomads were arrested in April 2003.

items.label: Quebec eradicated more cannabis plants than BC in 2003; Hells Angels 'likely dominant in Québec'
items.detail: RCMP data cited by NDIC: Quebec 579,381 plants and 11,327 lb processed; BC 460,971 plants. 'Hells Angels OMG is likely dominant in Québec, where RCMP reports a trend toward outdoor grows.' Canadian marijuana now commonly smuggled into New York and Vermont, among other states.

items.label: Vermont's hard-drug supply came from southern New England and New York, not Quebec
items.detail: Local dealers bought powder cocaine and heroin from Dominican groups in Holyoke, Lawrence, Lowell, Springfield, Hartford and NYC. Crack was sold by MA/CT/NY groups. Only 'small quantities' of cocaine, and smaller heroin amounts from Montreal, crossed from Canada. No Quebec-versus-New York conflict reported.

items.label: No documented Quebec–New York turf war over the Vermont market (negative finding)
items.detail: NDIC 2002: marijuana trafficking in Vermont 'not typically associated' with violence, and no growers' traps reported. The NDIC 2003 and 2007 reports describe Canadian marijuana and New York/southern-New England crack/heroin as separate supply chains. I found no news, court record or assessment describing such a conflict in 2002–2005.

items.place: Franklin/Orleans Cos. VT; Clinton/Franklin Cos. NY
items.label: No smuggling-related violence or NYC-Quebec turf war found, 2002-2006
items.detail: Searches of NDIC, joint border assessments, D. Vt./NDNY opinions, the Quebec extradition judgment, Press-Republican, La Voix de l'Est, Seven Days and AP found no shootings, disappearances or bodies tied to cross-border smuggling in this area in 2002-2006, and no evidence of NYC dealers competing with Quebec suppliers. NYC buyers appear as customers. The Bedford cartel was a family/neighbour network (S16). Caveat: 2002-2006 local press archives are largely not indexed online. One unexplained death of a cooperating witness is noted in S15.

items.label: HEAT (Heroin Enforcement Action Team) launched
items.detail: Formed in August 2003 inside the VSP drug task force; it had already made 19 arrests, with 62 more planned in four communities. The commissioner said out-of-state groups saw VT as a 'ripe market'. A $170,000 Community Heroin Intervention Program went to Rutland, Burlington, Williston and Barre.

items.label: Armed backpack smugglers near the line
items.detail: Border Patrol caught a Swanton man and a Quebec man, both armed, 2 miles south of the border with 25 lb cached. The Quebec man got 10 years (100+ kg conspiracy, March–Sept 2003), and 12 Canadians and Vermonters were convicted.

items.label: Armed home invasion in Montgomery, over marijuana
items.detail: A masked crew of St. Albans men tied up a Montgomery woman, 60, threatened her with a shotgun, shot her dog and ransacked the house, wrongly believing she grew marijuana. Four were charged in February 2006 after a source came forward.

items.label: Richford pipeline: Canadian marijuana, cocaine swap
items.detail: The Northern Vermont Drug Task Force raided two Richford men (125 lb, $55,000, 14 guns, about 20 vehicles). Typical Canadian loads were about 200 lb and one was 500 lb; an informant claimed 1,500 lb a week. Another informant bought at $2,600/lb and traded the marijuana for cocaine in Massachusetts to resell in Richford.

items.label: Operation Hurricane: four cells working with the Hells Angels
items.detail: 31 people with Hells links arrested and $4.3M in assets frozen. Police said the cells were 'not an official part of the Hells Angels but they were working with them.' Charges included production and gangsterism.

items.label: Champlain IBET already operating by Nov 2003
items.detail: Joint DOJ / Solicitor General of Canada release: IBETs 'already operating' in border areas including St-Lawrence Valley Central, Valleyfield and Champlain; two new teams brought coverage to every strategic location on the border. No founding date given for Champlain.

items.label: Judge dismisses border pot case as 'federal'
items.detail: After a hung jury on a 10 lb border case, a judge dismissed it, noting Franklin County prosecutors handle about 33 cases a month against about 1 for federal prosecutors.

items.label: About 269 kg of powdered ecstasy declared as potato starch, from Antwerp
items.detail: CISC example of Port of Montreal used as an ecstasy-precursor and powder import point.

items.label: Vito Rizzuto arrested on a US (Bonanno) murder-conspiracy indictment
items.detail: Rizzuto was the only Canadian among 28 Bonanno arrests. CBC says he had brokered the alliance between the Mafia, Hells Angels, Rock Machine and street gangs. Extradited 2006. CISC 2004 notes possible changes in Mafia leadership in Ontario and Quebec.

items.label: Largest raids in three years against the Hells Angels network that took over after 2001
items.detail: 36 arrested after a 30-month probe into 'who would take over the drug trade.' After Springtime only 59 Hells were left free, 23 of them in the 'powerful Sherbrooke chapter, one of the gang's richest and most ruthless.' An ex-SQ expert predicted members would be brought in from Sherbrooke or Trois-Rivières to run the South and Montreal.

items.place: Highgate Springs POE; Swanton truck stop; St. Albans; stopped on Route 7 south of Burlington
items.label: Over 55 lb behind a false wall in a sawdust tractor-trailer
items.detail: A Canadian driver entered at Highgate Springs with a load of sawdust; a pickup from the same firm crossed 15 minutes earlier as an escort. ICE and VSP followed both via Swanton and St. Albans down I-89, then stopped the truck. Over 55 lb found behind a false front wall. Suppression motion denied (D. Vt. 2005). This was three weeks before the Maitland disappearance.

items.label: Richford Town Meeting: principal warns of open-air dealing; police department vote defeated
items.detail: Two weeks before Brianna vanished, the Richford Jr.-Sr. High School principal told ~130 voters at the March 1, 2004 Town Meeting informational session that brazen daytime drug dealing was happening on Main Street and in the school parking lot. On March 2, voters defeated the proposal to form a local police department, leaving Richford and neighbouring Montgomery reliant on Vermont State Police patrols from the St. Albans barracks and county sheriff contracts.

items.label: Sheldon mobile-home raid
items.detail: About two weeks before she vanished, St. Albans police raided a Sheldon mobile home; shots were fired and nearly 4 oz of cocaine seized. No link to her has been reported.

items.label: Counterfeit $10 bills passed in St. Albans
items.detail: Two St. Albans men, 18 and 19, arrested for passing home-printed $10 bills at local shops; deputies seized the computer used. No link to drugs, Quebec or the case (St. Albans Messenger, March 2004).

items.label: A snowmobile trail ends at the Black Lantern
items.detail: The VAST 120F feeder trail ends directly at the Black Lantern Inn, so riders can sled to its door (maintained in March 2004 by the Covered Bridge Snowmobile Club in Montgomery Center, 802-326-4687; adjacent corridors maintained by the Missisquoi Bearcats in Richford, 802-933-4369, Cold Hollow Barons in Enosburg Falls, 802-933-4123, and Borderline Ridge Riders in Alburg, 802-796-3746). Snow at Enosburg Falls was a trace to 3 in on 17-21 March 2004, so the valley-floor feeder was probably thin or bare that night.

items.label: A marijuana-leaf trinket hung from her visor
items.detail: A green plastic leaf on a black cord hung from the sun visor; it shows in the travellers' photo of the car that morning. A common teen accessory of the time; on its own it says nothing about the trade.
items.source: Bob Kates, BobKat's Lair (2013, 2018) and True Crime Twins (2018), via casegraph media

items.label: Brianna Maitland vanishes
items.detail: She leaves the Black Lantern Inn about 11:20 pm; her car is found backed into the old Dutchburn house on VT-118.

items.label: Berkshire raid on the tip she was held there
items.detail: Police raid a house rented by two men described as New York drug dealers; drugs and guns found, no sign of her. One was later arrested in New York City; his plea required cooperation.

items.label: 14-defendant NY/MA/VT crack ring sentenced
items.detail: The leader, a Queensbury, NY man, 28, with Springfield ties, got 10 years federally. He travelled to Rutland regularly for about 3 years, making about $5,500 a trip and selling from motels and safe houses.

items.label: 'First meth lab in Vermont' (2 g)
items.detail: Two men from Missouri/Arkansas were arrested cooking about 2 g. The task force commander called it the first lab they knew of in VT. A second Rutland County lab was found within the year.

items.label: 2004 binational assessment: pot south, cocaine north, HAMC
items.detail: Marijuana mostly southbound and cocaine mostly northbound. Canadian groups sometimes trade 4–8 lb of marijuana for 1 kg of cocaine. The Hells Angels and Asian groups were the main cross-border marijuana and MDMA smugglers; Quebec MDMA labs were increasing.

items.label: St. Albans crack network, 10+ kg, Holyoke powder
items.detail: A St. Albans resident ran couriers distributing over 10 kg of crack from 2004 to March 2006, cooking Holyoke-bought powder at home. $170,000+ was seized from floor joists, tyre-slashing was used to enforce payment, and she got 168 months (the judge's 'largest crack case').

items.label: CISC 2004: four stable Quebec Hells Angels chapters; 100% conviction rate in megatrials
items.detail: 34 chapters in Canada, two Quebec chapters inactive; about 500 members nationally. 'The Quebec HELLS ANGELS still remain criminally active with four stable chapters.' Arrests may let street gangs expand. Drug income now includes 'increasingly methamphetamine'.

items.label: CISC: reserve-based brokers smuggle across the border for the Hells Angels and Asian groups
items.detail: Aboriginal brokers in southern Ontario and Quebec, 'often associated to Asian-based networks or the HELLS ANGELS', smuggle marijuana, currency and people. Movement is often 'on contract for other organized crime groups based in Ontario and Quebec'.

items.label: CISC: two-way trade — cocaine and guns north, marijuana and cash south
items.detail: 'Cocaine transits the U.S. ... and is subsequently smuggled into Canada. In return, illicit drugs, such as marihuana, currency and people are smuggled into the U.S.' Firearms bought legally in the US are diverted to Canadian criminals.

items.label: Akwesasne smuggling ring: 12 arrested on both sides of the border
items.detail: The leader allegedly moved about $4M a year of drugs from Canada into the US. A New York police dispatcher was charged with tipping off the ring.

items.place: Lower St. Lawrence, Laval, Lower Laurentians; New Brunswick/Maine border
items.label: Quebec-grown marijuana exported to US through New Brunswick
items.detail: SQ investigation begun 2004 (Rimouski). March 2007 searches seized 9,567 plants and 93.85 kg; May 2007 sweep with 73 arrest warrants. Notes rising smuggling across the Maine–New Brunswick border to large US cities.

items.label: VSP: two people said she owed money for drugs
items.detail: Press conference: foul play may be involved; two people said she owed a dealer money. By 2008 VSP said the drug link could not be substantiated and was largely rumour.

items.label: Killing of Ligia Rae Collins, 25, local crack dealer
items.detail: A Burlington woman, 38, confessed to beating her crack dealer with a bat. Police said she was broke and desperate for crack; the defence said the fight was about child care and a gun. Her boyfriend dumped the body in Ripton and later shot himself. Collins's boyfriend, who reported her missing on July 5, was one of the two men arrested in the April 15, 2004 Berkshire drug raid; a later third-hand hearsay claim by the convicted killer's relative attempting to link the case to Brianna was never corroborated by VSP.

items.label: State-funded treatment clients 4,500 to 7,741
items.detail: A Douglas administration op-ed said state-sponsored substance-abuse treatment clients grew from about 4,500 (about 1999) to 7,741 (2003).

items.label: 180–190 lb in car-carrier truck at Highgate Springs
items.detail: Two Quebec truckers (Laval area), bound for Boston, were each to be paid $40,000 to bring in marijuana hidden under the trailer's car racks. Both pleaded guilty in Dec 2004.

items.label: Mafia position: sophisticated, top-tier importer, works with bikers
items.detail: CISC: Montreal Mafia 'highly influential'. It stays 'at the upper echelon of illicit drug importation and distribution', and its drugs include cocaine, hashish, ecstasy and, more recently, marijuana grown in Canada. Some Hells Angels in Quebec have links to Mafia members.

items.label: CISC: Montreal street gangs (mostly Caribbean-based) moving into space left by biker arrests
items.detail: 2003: 'Successful operations against OMGs in Quebec and Ontario have enabled street gangs to expand their share of the illicit drug market.' 2004: two major Quebec gangs are now active in Ontario and can exploit Hells Angels weaknesses.

items.label: Canadian precursor controls (2003) cut the pseudoephedrine pipeline; Canadian meth labs rising
items.detail: NDIC: superlabs fell from 246 (2001) to 133 (2003), likely because bulk Canadian pseudoephedrine was harder to get. Canadian meth-lab seizures went 13 (2001), 25 (2002), 39 (2003); producers were bikers, Asian groups and independents. Meth smuggling from Canada into the US was 'very low'.

items.place: Rural path through Derby Line VT (Orleans County); pickup at I-91 Exit 29
items.label: About 15 groups walked a rural Derby Line path in 2 months
items.detail: Between Aug and Oct 2004 about 15 groups of migrants (Pakistan, India, South America) crossed on foot by one rural path; 7 groups intercepted; guides escaped; pickups at I-91 Exit 29. Shows how porous the Orleans County foot routes were in 2004 (not a drug case).

items.place: Lost Nation Rd / Frontier Rd, Clinton County NY; pickup at a country store near the Franklin County line (Burke station)
items.label: Three backpackers with 50-lb duffels met by cars rented in Manhattan
items.detail: A sensor caught a 4 a.m. crossing on foot. Three carriers, each with a 50-lb bag (two fled), were to be met by two cars rented in Manhattan the day before, cover story a casino trip back to NYC. The court describes the method: foot carrier, a load car and a scout car, and walkie-talkies because cell phones fail near the border. The carrier said he had done it four times; one run six months earlier was aborted. NDNY indictment: 50+ kg conspiracy.

items.label: 2003 homicides double; Franklin crime up
items.detail: 17 homicides in 2003 against 8 in 2002; Franklin was one of four counties with rising crime. The commissioner blamed a 'culture of violence… as a result of drug dealers coming into the state.'

items.label: Joint 2004 assessment: Canadian marijuana mostly bud; production growing in Quebec
items.detail: RCMP estimates 960-2,400 t of Canadian marijuana a year; mostly BC, but 'significant' production now in Ontario and Quebec. Southbound seizures mainly bud (sinsemilla). Marijuana entering the US from Canada: 4.4 t (FY2001), 12.2 t (FY2002), 15.8 t (FY2003). US enforcement on the northern border 'remains far below other U.S. border regions'.

items.label: THC: Canadian samples about 8-10%, not the reported 20%
items.detail: Average THC in Canadian samples (bud only): 8.7% (2001), 8.3% (2002), 9.6% (2003); only 0.5% of over 15,000 samples since 1989 reached 20% or more. US sinsemilla: 7.9%, 7.3%, 7.4%.

items.label: Cocaine mostly moves north; marijuana traded for cocaine
items.detail: Proceeds from Canadian marijuana sold in the US sometimes buy cocaine to smuggle north; DEA reports 4-8 lb of Canadian marijuana traded per kg of cocaine. Cocaine moves both ways but mostly north. Colombian and Italian groups are the main suppliers to eastern Canada, with outlaw bikers as wholesalers.

items.label: Cash smuggled between ports by backpackers, boats, snowmobiles
items.detail: Currency moves through ports in vehicles (sometimes in gas tanks), by parcel and bus couriers, and between ports by backpackers, boats and snowmobiles. FY2003: about $2M undeclared outbound and $4.3M inbound seized along the whole border.

items.place: Champlain NY POE; Lacolle QC POE
items.label: Champlain among top ports for US-bound MDMA from Canada
items.detail: US border ecstasy seizures: 7.27M doses (2000), 7.26M (2001), 3.91M (2002); most US-bound seizures from Canada were at Detroit, Champlain NY and Sumas WA. Canadian MDMA labs dismantled: 6 (2000), 8 (2001), 11 (2002), 12 (2003), in BC, Ontario and Quebec. June 2003: CBSA seized 5,180 tablets going into Canada at Lacolle.

items.place: Newport VT Border Patrol Station (Orleans County)
items.label: Agents released a smuggling suspect to use as an informant; reports falsified
items.detail: Three Newport agents arrested a drug-smuggling suspect and seized 60 lb of marijuana, then released him and wrote that the drugs were found 'abandoned' so they could use him as an informant. They cited a prior Newport practice. Two were indicted Nov 2005; charges against one dropped July 2006. Shows informant handling in the Swanton Sector at the time.

items.label: NDTA 2005: duffel loads of 40-100 lb typical, loads growing
items.detail: Overland loads from Canada typically ranged from personal-use amounts to 40-100 lb carried in duffel bags, but increasingly move in vehicles, often 200 lb or more. RCMP: production dominated by organized crime, notably Hells Angels and Vietnamese groups. 2002 potency: sinsemilla averaged 11.43% THC.

items.label: Meth lab first-responder training
items.detail: AP: two labs discovered in Rutland County in the past year, after years with none.

items.label: Salon: Canadian Hells Angels chapters among the largest coordinators of the cross-border pot trade
items.detail: Marijuana 'commonly bartered for cocaine and guns, which travel in the opposite direction, north into Canada'. BC Bud traded at over $3,000 a pound. The article is BC-focused.

items.label: Franklin County drug/narcotic offences 137 to 217
items.detail: City grant application tables: county drug offences 137 (2005), 203 and 217 in the next two columns (header partly illegible, likely 2006–07). St. Albans City: 39, 87, 93. Also mentions Latin Kings, Bloods and Los Solidos members living locally but not organised.

items.label: RCMP Drug Situation Report 2005: Quebec seized 700,000 plants; marijuana bartered for cocaine and guns
items.detail: 'Currency, firearms and cocaine are smuggled back into Canada in exchange for Canadian-grown marihuana.' Outlaw bikers and Asian groups dominate. Quebec labs specialise in methamphetamine 'logo tablets' sold at raves.

items.place: Bedford, Saint-Armand, Philipsburg, Frelighsburg (Brome-Missisquoi, on the Vermont line)
items.label: Project CURE: farm-based marijuana export ring dismantled (Sherbrooke Record, 9 June 2005)
items.detail: About 250 officers from the SQ, RCMP, Vermont State Police and DEA raided 19 Canadian sites; 34 arrested and about $5.5M in assets seized in Canada. Pot was grown on farm fields, and landowners were paid or threatened. A helicopter was used to scout fields, including other growers' patches to steal from. Loads crossed by foot carriers and commercial trucks, 'thousands of kilos'. Eleven were to be extradited to Vermont for importing 1,000+ kg; US evidence dated to 1991. SQ: 'no clear link to biker gangs or other known organized crime groups.' A relative of the alleged leader was shot dead in Frelighsburg about 1999; the shooter was never found.

items.label: RCMP 2005: 51 synthetic-drug labs seized nationally, all ecstasy labs 'super' labs
items.detail: 17 ecstasy labs (15 MDMA, 2 MDA) and about 29 meth labs. Ecstasy is bartered across the border for firearms and other drugs.

items.label: About 5.8 lb heroin at Champlain
items.detail: Attempted import of heroin from Canada; search recorded on the port's security cameras; NDNY indictment 1:05-CR-487, opinion Feb 2006 (419 F.Supp.2d 242).

items.place: Mooers Corner NY (Champlain Station, Swanton Sector)
items.label: About 261 lb ecstasy after a sensor alert
items.detail: Search snippet of a June 2005 Border Patrol release: Champlain Station agents stopped a vehicle after an electronic intrusion alert; a dog alert led to about 261 lb of ecstasy. Original page could not be opened.

items.label: FY2005 to date: 4,067 lb marijuana, 291 lb ecstasy, $1.467M
items.detail: Search snippet of the same June 2005 release: Oct 1 2004 to June 23 2005 sector seizures. Original page could not be opened.

items.place: Saint-Armand / Bedford / Frelighsburg QC (across from Franklin County VT)
items.label: 'Bedford cartel': cornfield grows, runners carry duffels into the US
items.detail: Coordinated Canadian-US investigation of marijuana production in the Saint-Armand–Bedford region on the Vermont border. Method: starter plants grown indoors in spring, planted in cornfields, harvested Sept-Oct, then hired runners smuggle the product into the US, typically in duffel bags. About 40 Canadian residents arrested June 2005; 24 charged in Canada; 11 sought by the US for trial in Vermont federal court. Conspiracy period alleged: Jan 1 1991 to May 26 2005.

items.label: Alternative tally: 40 arrested incl. 7 farmers; 20,000 plants, 78 guns
items.detail: Snippet only (page blocked): June 8 2005 arrests of 40 people including 7 farmers; 20,000 plants, 78 firearms, 6 vehicles, a helicopter and $700,000. Conflicts with La Voix de l'Est's 7,500 plants.

items.place: Ontario, Quebec, New Brunswick → New England
items.label: NDIC 2007 New England: high-potency marijuana 'destined for U.S. markets via brokers operating in the Montreal area'
items.detail: Multi-thousand-plant grows in Ontario, Quebec and New Brunswick. Canada-based Asian groups and outlaw bikers smuggle hydroponic marijuana and MDMA into New England and send millions of dollars back. Separately, southern New England and NYC street gangs are expanding crack sales into rural northern New England, so the two networks sell different drugs.

items.label: Montgomery double murder by would-be marijuana buyers
items.detail: Two people from Connecticut came north asking around for 10 lb of marijuana to resell, and shot two Montgomery residents off Route 242 when told there was none. The prosecutor said there was no evidence the victim dealt.

items.label: Richford–Enosburg ring 2000–04: cash north in tyres
items.detail: Leaders from Richford and Enosburg pleaded guilty (1,000+ kg conspiracy, money laundering), and 14 defendants pleaded in total. Loads up to 1,000 lb (more than $1.5M wholesale) came by foot or grain truck. Payments of $500,000–750,000 were hidden in tyres driven to Canada.

items.label: Same case: the suspect described as a Canadian man
items.detail: Advocacy blog account of the Nov 2005 indictment: the agents took a Canadian man and his marijuana to the Newport station and let him go once he promised to inform. Not independently confirmed.

items.label: Crack Down Posse / Syndicate: street gang loyal to the Hells Angels (Operation Axe)
items.detail: Operation Axe began January 2006 against the Syndicate, formerly the Crack Down Posse, a Haitian street gang loyal to the Hells Angels. Its leader was a former Boucher bodyguard. 47 arrests in February 2009.

items.place: Highgate Springs VT POE; Burlington area
items.label: 34 lb in a gas tank; courier paid at the Montreal casino
items.detail: DEA Burlington investigation of a Burlington-area marijuana conspiracy (about 20 targets in VT, NY and Canada) began fall 2005. In Jan 2006 a car seen at the suspected distributor's home was stopped at Highgate Springs with 34 lb in the gas tank; the driver said a man at the Casino de Montréal paid him to smuggle marijuana into Vermont. The suspected distributor had 44 documented US entries, mostly at Highgate Springs.

items.label: NDTA 2006: northern-border seizure incidents peak in 2004
items.detail: Arrival-zone marijuana seizures on the northern border: 3,601 kg/42 incidents (2001), 8,370/73 (2002), 11,183/70 (2003), 9,236/166 (2004). Asian groups are expanding wholesale distribution of Canadian high-potency marijuana. Share of seized samples with THC of 5% or more: 15.8% (1989) to 60.0% (2005).

items.label: Amsterdam ecstasy ring exposed at Highgate
items.detail: Courier arrests at Highgate Springs started a case against a Dutch ring that shipped 100,000+ doses to NYC, Boston and Miami (1999). The leader got 20 years in 2004; 14+ pleas.

items.label: VDTF: weekly Massachusetts cocaine shipments to St. Albans
items.detail: Four were arrested after a 3-month probe, two women outside a St. Albans bar. Police described large weekly powder shipments from Massachusetts, sold as powder and crack. This appears to be the same network as the item above.

items.label: Bodypacked Springfield heroin bound for Burlington
items.detail: Two Vermonters (from Lowell and Burlington) carried about 160 bags' worth internally. They said they bought it in Springfield, MA at $45/g; police valued it at $30–40 a bag in VT.

items.label: Prescription opioids overtake heroin in treatment, 2006
items.detail: In 2006, other opiates including OxyContin surpassed heroin as the primary opioid among clients of ADAP-funded treatment programs.

items.place: Sherbrooke area; Magog; Kanesatake; crossings at Coaticook (QC) and Cornwall (ON)
items.label: RCMP breaks a ring exporting about 100 lb of cannabis a week to the US, linked to Hells Angels chapters
items.detail: 36 arrested; 24 of 42 searches were in the Sherbrooke area. The alleged organiser was a Kanesatake woman. Two former Magog police officers were among those arrested. 'Close links' to the Montreal, Sherbrooke and Trois-Rivières Hells Angels chapters. US$4.8M laundered January–May 2006; $1M cash and an AK-47 seized. Most exporting was done from the Sherbrooke area.

items.label: Extradition of 11 Bedford-area residents to Vermont refused
items.detail: Judge discharged all 11 (2006 QCCS 4211), finding no admissible proof they belonged to the broad conspiracies alleged; wiretap summaries in the US record were excluded. The judgment notes cooperating witness CW-14 'had recently died' (US letter July 4, 2006); no cause given.

items.place: Akwesasne / St. Lawrence River; loads to Burlington VT and East Coast
items.label: Cornwall-led ring: 22,000 lb by speedboat and snowmobile, 2005-2008
items.detail: 34 indicted Nov 2008. Speedboats, personal watercraft and fishing boats in summer, and snowmobiles with sleds in winter, crossed the St. Lawrence at the reservation. Loads of 100-120 lb went in car trunks to East Coast points including Burlington. A ledger showed $700,000 in 9 days in May 2006. Over 800 lb and over $2M seized from lower-level members 2005-08.

items.label: NDTA 2007: Canada-based Asian groups replace Israeli MDMA networks
items.detail: Since 2004, Canada-based Asian (mainly Vietnamese and Chinese) groups have expanded MDMA distribution, mostly by vehicle through US-Canada land ports. MDMA seized in northern-border states except NY: 160,228 doses (2001), 152,312 (2002), 34,416 (2003), 587,455 (2004), 2,263,040 (2005).

items.label: Project Colisée: nearly 100 Rizzuto-clan suspects arrested
items.detail: Four-year probe; 1,300 charges, including cocaine importation; airport employees arrested; over $3M seized.

items.label: Border marijuana seizures 419 lb (2000) to 3,000+ lb (2005)
items.detail: DHS credited post-9/11 checkpoints with a jump in northern New England marijuana seizures. Civil-liberties critics objected to interior I-89/I-91 checkpoints.

items.label: Operation Granite Streets: largest VSP sweep
items.detail: 25 arrested (30+ eventually) for crack, cocaine and heroin. Most were local; police said buyers no longer needed to go to MA or NY. The operation followed the September 2006 Saunders homicide over a bad drug deal.

items.label: 117 lb and US/Canadian cash in a Snye home
items.detail: Akwesasne Mohawk Police search warrant from a joint investigation into drugs and cash moving onto the territory; one man, 41, arrested.

items.place: New England HIDTA incl. Chittenden, VT
items.label: NE HIDTA 2007: MA street gangs expand crack into VT; debt violence
items.detail: Massachusetts gangs travel to VT with crack, sell from hotels or local women's homes, and some NYC gang members relocate to rural areas. VT officials reported robberies, thefts and shootings over unpaid drug debts, and traffickers murdered for proceeds.

items.label: Canadian hiding in a car trunk with about $345,000 going north
items.detail: Same Burlington conspiracy: ICE at Rouses Point stopped a vehicle trying to re-enter Canada with a Canadian citizen hidden in the trunk with about $345,000. Shows proceeds flowing north to Quebec.

items.label: NDTA 2008: marijuana seized at/between US-Canada ports, 2001-2006
items.detail: 3,549 kg (2001), 7,851 (2002), 10,288 (2003), 4,147 (2004), 9,458 (2005), 4,170 (2006). NDIC notes seizures show no clear trend despite reports of rising smuggling.

items.label: Federal MDMA seizures in Vermont jump 2003-2005
items.detail: Vermont: 31 doses (2002), 17,811 (2003), 47,879 (2004), 56,437 (2005), 26,240 (2006). New York: 2.79M, 413,658, 740,546, 1.25M, 1.14M. New Hampshire: 0, 0, 2,633, 9,517, 1. Canada now reported as the primary MDMA source for US markets.

items.label: RCMP pill lab (just outside the 2002–2006 window, for scale)
items.detail: 44,000 ecstasy pills, 83,000 meth capsules, 35 kg MDMA powder, 32 kg meth powder. This is the closest well-documented Quebec lab bust I could open; none confirmed in Townships/Montérégie for 2002–2006.

items.label: VSP: no active Hells Angels chapter in Vermont; worry over Canadian hydroponic marijuana
items.detail: A VSP major told the Senate Judiciary Committee Vermont had no active Hells Angels chapter, but feared high-grade hydroponic marijuana grown by Canadian Hells Angels would reach the state more often if one formed.

items.label: Commissioner: dealers see VT as a market to 'take over'
items.detail: Out-of-state dealers from NH, NY, MA, CT and DE come for higher margins, some tied to gangs, and may see VT as a market to take over. The 2007 Franklin County spree was tied to crack and pills with New York links. Marijuana profits go to organised crime and OMGs. Meth-laced ecstasy from Canada was emerging.

items.place: New England HIDTA incl. Chittenden, VT
items.label: NE HIDTA 2008: Montreal/Toronto supply marijuana, MDMA, pills
items.detail: Canada-based traffickers in Montreal and Toronto smuggle marijuana, MDMA and prescription drugs, and the region is a transit zone. Crack in Burlington grew via southern New England and NYC groups. 2 meth labs and 1 MDMA/meth lab were seized in VT in 2007.

items.label: 'Bedford gang' trial: jury rejects gangsterism; export charges dropped
items.detail: Of 9 accused in the first trial, 7 were acquitted, and the gangsterism and marijuana-export charges fell. A judge had earlier (2006) refused to extradite the leader and 10 others to the US. Defence: 'no general conspiracy, just small conspiracies between individuals'.

items.label: St. Albans 7-year trend; Montreal and NY 'source areas'
items.detail: The police chief testified to +186% drug investigations/warrants and +125% assaults/robberies over 7 years. Montreal and New York are 'traditionally source areas'. Out-of-state urban dealers were arriving and some had been pushed out of Burlington. In Jan–Feb 2007 NYC men ran a crack house three doors from the police station.

items.place: Highgate Springs VT; Alburgh VT; Fort Covington and North Hudson NY
items.label: Ecstasy route shifts east to the Lake Champlain corridor in 2007-08 (later context)
items.detail: 200,000 tablets seized at Highgate Springs on Nov 26 2008 (largest ground seizure in New England); a Montreal man with about 60,000 at Alburgh in Oct 2008 had made up to 25 Canada-NYC trips. Border Patrol ecstasy seizures: 5 on the northern border in 2007 (3 in Swanton Sector); 5 in 2008 (4 in Swanton). Shows the large ecstasy flow through Franklin County came after 2006.

items.label: Single goal: making money for the Bedford cartel (La Voix de l'Est)
items.detail: Crown said the evidence would not involve bikers, the Italian Mafia or street gangs. The accused were tied by family, friendship or neighbourhood. Investigation began 2003. $260,000 cash found hidden in paint cans in Saint-Armand.

items.label: Projet Cure (from 2003): prosecutor says no bikers, mafia or street gangs
items.detail: At the opening of the trial of 8 accused, the Crown said the 'Bedford cartel' members were linked by family, friendship or neighbourhood and wanted only to make money, with no ties to outlaw bikers, the Italian mafia or street gangs. The Projet Cure investigation began in 2003. $260,000 cash was found buried in paint cans at the leader's Saint-Armand home in June 2005.

items.place: Franklin, Clinton and St. Lawrence Counties NY
items.label: Nearest documented smuggling violence is after 2006
items.detail: Franklin County DA and DEA: before 2007 arrests, a Malone family importing about $4M of pot burned a rip-off associate's vehicle in Schenectady. In 2008 a courier in a Russian organized-crime case was shot dead at home in Stockholm (St. Lawrence County) by fellow gang members. Around 2010 a snowmobile hauler fired at a surveillance helicopter. Smugglers watched Mohawk police officers' homes on the Canadian side. No 2002-2006 incidents cited.

items.label: Bedford cartel trial: six accused guilty (La Voix de l'Est)
items.detail: The family head was convicted of production, trafficking, conspiracy and gangsterism; 6 of 8 accused were found guilty. The network allegedly produced and sold more than 1,000 kg a year, notably to the US. The June 2005 seizure was 7,500 plants plus a helicopter and guns, about $5M in all.

items.label: Six convicted; police say over 1,000 kg a year sold, some to the US
items.detail: Sûreté du Québec, RCMP and US agents seized 7,500 plants plus assets including a helicopter and firearms (about $5M) in June 2005. Police: the cartel produced and sold over 1,000 kg a year, including to the United States. Six found guilty, including of gangsterism.

items.place: Quebec to New York City (via ports and indigenous territory)
items.label: Laval-based network supplying NYC worked with the Mafia, not against it
items.detail: A Quebec trafficker (27 years, EDNY 2014) ran a network moving about 450 kg of marijuana a week into New York at its peak, with Hells Angels hauling BC hydroponic product and ties to the Bonanno and Rizzuto crime families. Proceeds bought Sinaloa cocaine sent to Canada. He corrupted port officials and used indigenous lands. A cooperative NYC-Quebec supply chain, not a turf war.

items.label: Douglas on DETER: 26 troopers, HEAT, 11 recovery centres
items.detail: The former governor listed DETER's components: a counsellor in every middle and high school, an 80-bed facility, 11 recovery centres, 26 State Police vacancies filled, enhanced trafficking penalties, and the HEAT undercover unit.

items.label: Later account of methods: ghillie suits, night vision, duffels, scouts
items.detail: Game-camera images of carriers in white ghillie suits and night-vision goggles with duffel bags; crews seen in body armour; scout drivers relay agents' positions. The sector chief linked them to Quebec motorcycle gangs' hydroponic grows. Shows how the backpack method later developed.

snowmobile.smuggling_context: Federal drug assessments (NDIC 2003 Vermont Drug Threat Assessment, datasets/drugs/us.json 'ndic03-marijuana-hells') document that Hells Angels-linked Quebec networks smuggled hydroponic 'Quebec Gold' (M-39) marijuana across the northern Vermont border via snowmobiles in winter and low-flying helicopters—including a 28 Feb 2003 drop of 250 lb of 'Quebec Gold' from a helicopter onto a snowmobile trail in adjacent Lowell, VT ('lowell-helicopter').

snowmobile.ask_investigators: Were VAST 120/120F open on 19-20 March 2004? Did anyone arrive at the Black Lantern by sled that night? The 2004 grooming logs and VAST closure notices of the Covered Bridge Snowmobile Club (Montgomery Center, 802-326-4687), Missisquoi Bearcats (Richford, 802-933-4369), and Cold Hollow Barons (Enosburg Falls, 802-933-4123) would say; groomers often run at night.

ski_buses.why_it_matters: Each Saturday morning bus on the Burlington, Montreal and Plattsburgh routes made a scheduled run past the car between roughly 08:30 and 08:45 while it sat backed into the Dutchburn house, and an afternoon return after 16:00. A professional motorcoach driver sitting in an elevated cab on a fixed timetable is the best-placed witness to the car's state between dawn and the travellers' 10:15 photos. Bus charter operator, dispatch manifests and driver names would be in Jay Peak's or the charter contractor's 2004 records.
ski_buses.ask_investigators: Did Jay Peak's Burlington, Montreal and Plattsburgh weekend buses run on Saturday 20 March 2004? Which charter company operated each route, what were the exact crossing/arrival times, and were the drivers ever asked what they saw at the Dutchburn house around 08:35 am?

groups.group: Milk tankers and overnight dairy hands
groups.evidence: Franklin County had 315 dairy farms in 2002 (data/area_businesses_2004.json). Tanker pickups run daily or every other day, mostly 6 am-6 pm (datasets/trucking/trucking.json). In addition, a March 2004 St. Albans Messenger classified ad (samessenger.com/1025.html; archive/gemini_antigravity/raw/sam_classifieds_mar2004.txt) sought a full-time '9pm - 6am' night milker at 2864 East Berkshire Rd. (about 5 km west of the Dutchburn house), confirming overnight dairy workers commuted on VT-118/VT-105 at the exact start and end of the night window.
groups.ask: St. Albans Cooperative Creamery hauler route sheets for 20 Mar 2004 (which tanker served farms on VT-118 near Dutchburn Farm Road and at what time) and overnight milking staff at large East Berkshire / Montgomery dairy operations.

groups.evidence: Saturday routine deliveries are uncommon; emergency calls possible on a cold night (8-15 F).
groups.ask: Local dealers' 2004 delivery tickets for VT-118 addresses on 20 Mar, if retained.

groups.group: Jay Peak night crews, Montgomery bar patrons and early-morning skiers
groups.evidence: Jay Peak was a top-10 area employer in 2004 (data/area_businesses_2004.json). Groomers and snowmakers work nights; staff and Friday-night bar patrons heading home west to Enosburg, Sheldon or St. Albans drive VT-242, Montgomery Center and VT-118 past the house: the same direction the witnesses' Civic came from. FirstTracksOnline 'No Bull' reports (3462.html, 3560.html, 3650.html; archive/gemini_antigravity/raw/ski_threads_full_2004.txt) confirm out-of-area skiers drank after-hours in Montgomery bars (The Belfry, The Lodge, The Snowshoe, Black Lantern Inn) and lodged in Sutton, QC (La Paimpolaise) before crossing the border in the morning to ski Jay Peak, while weekend powder hunters drove north starting at 3:30 am on Saturday 20 March (NASIOC t=519715/541603; FirstTracksOnline 3650.html; ZoneSki t=1065).
groups.ask: Jay Peak's 2004 grooming and night-shift rosters and lounge closing time on 19 Mar; staff who lived west of Montgomery; credit-card receipts from Montgomery bars on 19 Mar.

groups.evidence: Northwestern Medical Center, St. Albans (560 staff) and North Country Hospital, Newport (505) ran round-the-clock shifts; Franklin Foods (Enosburg Falls, 10.9 km) and Blue Seal Feeds (Richford, 9.2 km) are the nearest plants. A worker living around Montgomery and starting an 11 pm or midnight shift west of town, or ending a 7 am shift, drives VT-118 in the windows.
groups.ask: 2004 shift times at these employers; whether employees commuting on VT-118 were canvassed.

groups.evidence: Swanton Sector Border Patrol and the Richford, East Richford and West Berkshire ports sit 9-15 km north (data/area_businesses_2004.json; ledger/places.json). Agents patrol back roads near the border at night and log vehicle checks; port officers change shifts around midnight.
groups.ask: Border Patrol Richford station patrol logs, vehicle checks and sensor hits for 19-20 Mar 2004; port shift rosters; whether agents passed VT-118 that night.
